งานที่ทำซ้ำบ่อย เช่น ขอให้สรุปประชุม เขียนคำขอถึงฝ่ายบริการ หรืออธิบายปัญหาทางเทคนิค ควรมีเทมเพลตของตัวเองแยกกัน เทมเพลตที่ดีกำหนดหัวข้อไว้ล่วงหน้า (เป้าหมาย สิ่งที่รู้แล้ว สิ่งที่ยังไม่รู้ รูปแบบคำตอบ) เวลาใช้จริงก็แค่เติมบริบทใหม่ลงไป ไม่ต้องคิดโครงใหม่ทุกครั้ง

en.title: Prompt Management: Organize AI Prompts You Can Reuse
en.meta: Manage AI prompts as a system: separate goal, facts and sources, save templates, keep versions and check personal details before pasting into any AI chat.
en.h1: Prompt management: store, reuse and check before you send
en.lead: Most people manage prompts by copying an old message from a past chat and tweaking it. A month later they cannot find it, or tell which version actually worked best.
en.answer: A manageable prompt always has three parts: the goal (what you want the AI to do), the context and facts (with where each came from), and the answer format. Save the reusable part as a template per type of task and swap only the context each time, keep older versions to compare, and check for personal details before every paste.
paras: The main problem with prompts is rarely wording; it is missing context. The AI answers wrongly because it does not know which document is the latest or which number is still unconfirmed. Writing facts as separate items, each tagged with its source, lets both you and the AI see what is reliable and what is still an open question.

Repeated tasks such as meeting summaries, support requests or technical problem reports deserve their own templates. A good template fixes the headings in advance (goal, what is known, what is unknown, answer format), so in practice you only add fresh context instead of rebuilding the structure.

Do not overwrite a prompt; keep versions. Edits often make results worse, and an earlier draft lets you roll back instantly. Finally, before pasting into any AI chat, scan for names, phone numbers, emails or account numbers that came along with screenshots or PDFs and decide whether to keep, replace or remove them.
look: Goal, facts and sources clearly separated
Several sources such as screenshots, PDFs, notes and copied text combined into one brief
Task-based templates to start quickly
Version history to go back to a draft that worked
Personal-detail detection before export, with you choosing to keep, replace or remove
steps: Write the goal as one sentence, e.g. “Summarize this proposal so my manager can read it in one minute.”
Collect every related source (screenshots, PDFs, notes, links) in one place.
Pull facts out as items, tag each with its source and flag any conflicts or uncertain points.
Pick the matching template, review personal details and save it as a new version.
Copy and paste into your AI chat; if the answer is off, fix the context rather than the wording.
rows: Are there templates per type of task?
No rebuilding the structure, more consistent results
Does every fact carry its source?
You can tell whether the AI was fed wrong information from the start
Can you review and handle personal details before export?
Screenshots and PDFs often contain names, phone or account numbers without you noticing
en.fits: AI Brief: AI Prompt from Files suits people who regularly hand real documents to an AI and want an organized brief instead of a long pasted blob. It turns screenshots, PDFs, files and notes into one brief with goal, facts and sources separated, keeps a confidence level for each fact, offers templates for technical problems, support requests, document analysis, study materials and meeting follow-ups, keeps version history, and runs text recognition and privacy detection on device. Detected details are never removed automatically; you decide on each one.
faq: Isn't a plain notes app enough to store prompts?
For a handful of prompts, yes. Once prompts need context from several documents, separating facts with sources, using templates and keeping version history makes them much faster to find and fix.
Do longer prompts give better AI answers?
Not necessarily. Relevant, well-sectioned context helps; length does not. Duplicated or conflicting information makes answers worse, so remove duplicates and flag conflicts before sending.
Which AI chats does AI Brief work with?
According to its store description, a finished brief is copied in one tap and pasted into any AI chat; it is not tied to one AI provider.

loc.title: Pancarte aéroport : quoi écrire pour être repéré sans exposer la personne
loc.meta: Pancarte d'accueil à l'aéroport : quel nom écrire, quelle taille de lettres, quelle couleur, et ce qu'il vaut mieux éviter (nom complet, hôtel, société).
loc.h1: Pancarte aéroport : le bon texte, la bonne taille, sans trop en dire
loc.lead: Dans un hall d'arrivée, la personne qui sort cherche son nom pendant deux ou trois secondes au milieu de dizaines de panneaux. Ce que vous écrivez compte autant que la taille.
loc.answer: Écrivez ce que la personne reconnaîtra instantanément : son nom de famille en majuscules, ou un prénom suivi de l'initiale (« MARIE D. »), éventuellement un mot de code convenu à l'avance. Évitez le nom complet associé à l'hôtel ou à l'entreprise. Visez des lettres d'au moins 8 à 10 cm de haut, un fort contraste (jaune ou blanc sur noir) et pas plus de deux lignes.
paras: Le nom de famille seul est la convention des chauffeurs professionnels : court, lisible de loin, et la personne le repère même fatiguée. Pour un proche ou un invité qui ne vous connaît pas, « Prénom + initiale » suffit. Un nom complet accompagné du nom de l'hôtel ou de la société, en revanche, donne à n'importe quel inconnu de quoi se présenter à votre place : c'est la raison pour laquelle de nombreuses agences recommandent un mot de code ou une version abrégée.

La lisibilité dépend surtout de la hauteur des lettres et du contraste. À une dizaine de mètres, des lettres de quelques centimètres sont illisibles ; il faut des caractères épais qui occupent toute la largeur. Un texte fixe se lit plus vite qu'un texte qui défile ; le défilement est utile seulement si le nom est trop long pour tenir en grand. Une couleur peu courante dans le hall aide aussi à se distinguer des autres panneaux blancs.

Si vous attendez plusieurs voyageurs ou si le vol est retardé, prévoyez de quoi alterner : le nom, puis une info pratique comme « SORTIE B » ou « TAXI ». Tenez le panneau à hauteur de poitrine, face aux portes de sortie, et restez au même endroit que celui communiqué par message.
look: Lettres assez grandes pour être lues à plusieurs mètres
Affichage fixe pour un nom court, défilant pour un texte plus long
Couleur de texte contrastée et différente des autres pancartes
Possibilité de tourner le texte pour occuper toute la hauteur de l'écran
Enchaîner plusieurs messages sans quitter le plein écran
steps: Convenez à l'avance du texte avec la personne : nom de famille, prénom + initiale ou mot de code.
Écrivez-le en majuscules, une seule ligne si possible, sans nom d'hôtel ni de société.
Choisissez une couleur vive sur fond sombre et réglez la taille au maximum lisible.
Vérifiez la lisibilité en posant l'écran à dix pas et en le regardant vous-même.
Placez-vous face aux portes, panneau à hauteur de poitrine, et envoyez votre position exacte par message.
rows: Nom de famille, prénom + initiale ou mot de code
Reconnu en un coup d'œil sans révéler trop d'informations
Lettres de 8 à 10 cm minimum, clair sur foncé
La personne vous cherche à plusieurs mètres, souvent fatiguée
Pouvoir alterner les noms ou ajouter une consigne
Évite de multiplier les feuilles et les confusions
loc.fits: LED Moving Text convient quand vous voulez transformer votre iPhone en pancarte d'accueil sans imprimer de feuille : on tape une phrase, on passe en plein écran, et elle se lit à travers le hall d'arrivée. L'aperçu sert d'éditeur pour régler texte, vitesse, taille et couleur ; le texte peut être fixe ou défilant, tourné de quatre-vingt-dix degrés pour occuper toute la hauteur, et la « Séquence de messages » fait défiler un message par ligne en direct ou avec une minuterie de 2 à 20 secondes. Pas de compte : vos messages restent sur l'iPhone.
faq: Faut-il écrire le nom complet sur la pancarte ?

Ce n'est pas nécessaire et c'est souvent déconseillé. Le nom de famille seul ou « Prénom + initiale » suffit pour être reconnu, et un mot de code convenu évite qu'un inconnu se présente à la place de la personne.
Un écran de téléphone est-il assez grand pour une pancarte ?

Pour un nom court, oui, à condition que les lettres remplissent l'écran : en tournant le texte pour utiliser toute la hauteur et en gardant un affichage fixe, un nom de cinq à huit lettres se lit de loin. Pour un nom long, le défilement aide.
Quelle couleur se voit le mieux dans un hall d'arrivée ?
Un texte clair et saturé (jaune, blanc, vert vif) sur fond noir offre le meilleur contraste. Choisir une couleur que les autres panneaux n'utilisent pas aide aussi à se démarquer.

en.title: Airport Arrival Sign: What to Write Without Oversharing
en.meta: Airport pickup sign tips: which name to write, letter size and colour, and what to avoid (full name plus hotel or company) so the right person spots you fast.
en.h1: Airport arrival sign: the right text, the right size, no oversharing
en.lead: In an arrivals hall, the person coming out scans dozens of signs for two or three seconds. What you write matters as much as how big it is.
en.answer: Write what the person will recognize instantly: their surname in capitals, or a first name plus initial (“MARIE D.”), or a code word agreed in advance. Avoid pairing the full name with the hotel or company. Aim for letters at least 8–10 cm tall, strong contrast (yellow or white on black) and no more than two lines.
paras: Surname only is the professional drivers' convention: short, readable from afar, and easy to spot even when tired. For a relative or a guest who has never met you, first name plus initial is enough. A full name with a hotel or company name, however, gives any stranger enough to introduce themselves in your place, which is why many agencies suggest a code word or a shortened form.

Readability depends mainly on letter height and contrast. From about ten metres, letters a few centimetres tall are unreadable; you need bold characters filling the full width. Static text reads faster than scrolling text; scrolling only helps when the name is too long to fit large. An unusual colour also helps you stand out from rows of white signs.

If you are meeting several travellers or the flight is delayed, plan to alternate: the name, then a practical note such as “EXIT B” or “TAXI”. Hold the sign at chest height facing the exit doors and stay at the exact spot you shared by message.
look: Letters large enough to read from several metres
Static display for a short name, scrolling for longer text
A contrasting text colour that differs from other signs
Rotating the text to use the full height of the screen
Moving through several messages without leaving full screen
steps: Agree on the text in advance: surname, first name plus initial, or a code word.
Write it in capitals, one line if possible, with no hotel or company name.
Pick a bright colour on a dark background and set the largest readable size.
Check readability by placing the screen ten steps away and looking yourself.
Stand facing the doors with the sign at chest height and message your exact position.
rows: Surname, first name plus initial, or code word
Recognized at a glance without revealing too much
Letters 8–10 cm minimum, light on dark
The traveller is looking from several metres, often tired
Ability to alternate names or add an instruction
Avoids juggling sheets of paper and mix-ups
en.fits: LED Moving Text fits when you want your iPhone to act as an arrival sign without printing anything: type a phrase, go full screen, and it reads across the arrivals hall. The preview is the editor for text, speed, size and colour; text can be static or scrolling, rotated ninety degrees to fill the full height, and Message Sequence shows one message per line, advanced live or on a 2–20 second timer. No account needed, and your messages stay on your iPhone.
faq: Should I write the full name on the sign?
It is not necessary and often discouraged. Surname only or first name plus initial is enough to be recognized, and an agreed code word stops a stranger from stepping in as the traveller.
Is a phone screen big enough for a pickup sign?

For a short name, yes, as long as the letters fill the screen: rotating the text to use the full height and keeping it static makes a five-to-eight-letter name readable from a distance. For a long name, scrolling helps.
Which colour stands out best in an arrivals hall?
Light, saturated text (yellow, white, bright green) on black gives the best contrast. Choosing a colour other signs are not using also helps you stand out.

loc.title: Thời tiết cho trẻ em: giờ nào nên cho bé ra ngoài khi nắng nóng và mưa rào
loc.meta: Cho bé ra ngoài lúc nào khi trời nóng ẩm: xem nhiệt độ cảm nhận, UV, khả năng mưa theo giờ; nên đi trước 9 giờ sáng hoặc sau 4 giờ chiều, mang ô.
loc.h1: Thời tiết cho trẻ em: chọn khung giờ ra ngoài an toàn trong ngày nóng và mưa
loc.lead: Ở Việt Nam, câu hỏi của phụ huynh thường không phải là “hôm nay bao nhiêu độ” mà là “mấy giờ thì đưa con ra công viên được, có kịp về trước cơn mưa chiều không”.
loc.answer: Với trẻ nhỏ, hãy xem ba chỉ số theo từng giờ thay vì chỉ nhìn nhiệt độ: nhiệt độ cảm nhận, chỉ số UV và khả năng mưa. Ngày nắng nóng, khung giờ hợp lý thường là trước 9 giờ sáng hoặc sau 4 giờ chiều, khi UV đã giảm. Khi UV từ 6 trở lên, cho bé đội mũ rộng vành, mặc áo mỏng dài tay và bôi kem chống nắng; mùa mưa thì kiểm tra khả năng mưa theo giờ và luôn mang ô hoặc áo mưa.
paras: Trẻ em nóng lên nhanh hơn người lớn và khó tự nói ra khi bị mệt vì nóng. Trong không khí ẩm, nhiệt độ cảm nhận có thể cao hơn nhiệt độ thực vài độ, nên một ngày 33°C có thể “cảm giác như” gần 40°C. Đó là con số nên dùng để quyết định thời gian chơi ngoài trời, chứ không phải nhiệt độ hiển thị lớn trên màn hình.

Chỉ số UV thường cao nhất trong khoảng 10 giờ sáng đến 3 giờ chiều, kể cả khi trời có mây. Theo khuyến nghị chung, từ mức UV 3 đã nên che chắn, từ mức 8 nên hạn chế ra ngoài giữa trưa. Trẻ dưới 6 tháng tuổi nên tránh nắng trực tiếp và dùng quần áo, bóng râm thay cho kem chống nắng; hãy hỏi bác sĩ nhi nếu bạn không chắc.

Mùa mưa ở nhiều nơi có kiểu mưa rào buổi chiều: sáng nắng gắt, chiều đổ mưa nhanh. Xem khả năng mưa theo từng giờ giúp bạn chọn đi chơi buổi sáng sớm và về nhà trước giờ mưa. Sau cơn mưa, không khí mát hơn nhưng đường trơn và có thể có sấm sét, nên chờ trời ổn định rồi mới ra lại.
look: Có nhiệt độ cảm nhận, không chỉ nhiệt độ thực
Có chỉ số UV và gợi ý khi nào cần kem chống nắng, mũ, kính râm
Có khả năng mưa và chi tiết theo từng giờ trong ngày
Gợi ý khung giờ phù hợp để ra ngoài
Báo trước khi trời sắp mưa hoặc khi ngày mai có thể mưa
steps: Buổi tối, xem dự báo ngày mai để biết có mưa hay không và nhiệt độ ra sao.
Buổi sáng, mở biểu đồ theo giờ và tìm khung giờ có nhiệt độ cảm nhận thấp, UV thấp và ít khả năng mưa.
Chuẩn bị theo chỉ số: mũ rộng vành và kem chống nắng khi UV cao, ô hoặc áo mưa khi khả năng mưa tăng, thêm nước uống.
Cho bé chơi ở nơi có bóng râm, nghỉ uống nước sau mỗi 15–20 phút khi trời nóng.
Theo dõi dấu hiệu mệt vì nóng (mặt đỏ, lừ đừ, ít đi tiểu) và đưa bé vào chỗ mát ngay nếu thấy.
rows: Nhiệt độ cảm nhận theo giờ
Độ ẩm làm cơ thể bé nóng hơn con số nhiệt độ thực
Chỉ số UV và giờ UV cao nhất
Da trẻ mỏng, dễ bị bỏng nắng kể cả khi trời có mây
Khả năng mưa theo từng giờ
Giúp đi và về trước cơn mưa, tránh sấm sét và đường trơn
loc.fits: Lumi Thời tiết: Dự báo mưa phù hợp với phụ huynh muốn biết nhanh hôm nay có nên đưa con ra ngoài không. Ứng dụng cho chỉ số ra ngoài từ 0 đến 100 tính từ nhiệt độ cảm nhận, khả năng mưa, chỉ số UV, gió và tình trạng bầu trời, chạm vào để xem từng yếu tố; gợi ý nên mặc gì, có cần mang ô, khi nào cần kem chống nắng, mũ hay kính râm, kèm danh sách đồ cần mang có thể chia sẻ. Có khung giờ lý tưởng để ra ngoài, biểu đồ nhiệt độ 24 giờ, dự báo 7 ngày và cảnh báo khi sắp mưa. Lưu ý: chỉ số dành cho việc ra ngoài nói chung, không phải tư vấn y tế riêng cho trẻ.
faq: Bao nhiêu độ thì không nên cho bé ra ngoài?

Không có một con số cố định, nhưng khi nhiệt độ cảm nhận vượt khoảng 35°C hoặc UV từ 8 trở lên, nên tránh cho bé chơi ngoài trời giữa trưa và chuyển sang sáng sớm hoặc chiều muộn, ở nơi có bóng râm và nhiều nước uống.
Trời nhiều mây có cần bôi kem chống nắng cho bé không?

Có. Tia UV vẫn xuyên qua mây, nên hãy xem chỉ số UV chứ không dựa vào việc trời có nắng hay không. Với trẻ dưới 6 tháng, ưu tiên bóng râm và quần áo che chắn, hỏi bác sĩ trước khi dùng kem chống nắng.
Lumi Thời tiết có báo trước khi sắp mưa không?
Có. Theo mô tả trên App Store, Lumi báo trước khi trời sắp mưa hoặc khi ngày mai có thể mưa, và có tiện ích trên Màn hình chính, Màn hình khóa cùng lời nhắc hằng ngày vào giờ bạn chọn.

en.title: Weather for Kids: When to Go Out in Tropical Heat and Showers
en.meta: When to take kids out in hot, humid weather: check feels-like temperature, UV and hourly rain chance; go before 9am or after 4pm, pack umbrella and sunscreen.
en.h1: Weather for kids: picking safe outdoor hours on hot, showery days
en.lead: In Vietnam, parents rarely ask “how hot is it today”. They ask “what time can I take my child to the park, and will we be home before the afternoon rain?”
en.answer: For young children, check three hourly numbers rather than temperature alone: feels-like temperature, UV index and chance of rain. On hot days the sensible windows are usually before 9am or after 4pm, once UV drops. At UV 6 or higher, use a wide-brimmed hat, thin long sleeves and sunscreen; in rainy season check the hourly rain chance and always carry an umbrella or raincoat.
paras: Children heat up faster than adults and rarely say when they are overheating. In humid air the feels-like temperature can run several degrees above the actual reading, so a 33°C day can feel close to 40°C. That is the number to use when deciding on outdoor play, not the big temperature on the screen.

UV is usually highest from about 10am to 3pm, even under cloud. General guidance is to start protecting skin from UV 3 and to limit midday time outdoors from UV 8. Babies under six months should stay out of direct sun, using clothing and shade rather than sunscreen; ask a paediatrician if unsure.

In many places the rainy season brings afternoon showers: harsh sun in the morning, a quick downpour later. Checking the hourly rain chance lets you go out early and get home before it hits. After rain the air is cooler, but paths are slippery and thunder may linger, so wait for conditions to settle.
look: Feels-like temperature, not just actual temperature
UV index with hints on when to use sunscreen, a hat or sunglasses
Chance of rain with hour-by-hour detail
A suggested best time window to go out
Alerts before rain or when tomorrow may be rainy
steps: In the evening, check tomorrow's forecast for rain and temperature.
In the morning, open the hourly chart and find a window with low feels-like temperature, low UV and low rain chance.
Pack by the numbers: hat and sunscreen for high UV, umbrella or raincoat when rain chance rises, plus water.
Keep play in the shade and take a drink break every 15–20 minutes in the heat.
Watch for heat strain (flushed face, sluggishness, peeing less) and move to a cool place right away if you see it.
rows: Humidity makes a child's body hotter than the actual reading
UV index and its peak hours
Young skin burns easily, even on cloudy days
Lets you go and return before the rain, avoiding thunder and slippery paths
en.fits: Lumi Weather: What to Wear suits parents who want a quick answer to whether today is a good day to take the kids out. It gives a 0–100 outing score built from feels-like temperature, rain chance, UV, wind and sky conditions, with a tap to see each factor; suggests what to wear, whether to take an umbrella and when sunscreen, a hat or sunglasses are needed, plus a shareable packing list. It shows the best time window to go out, a 24-hour temperature chart, a 7-day forecast and alerts before rain. Note that the score is for going out in general, not child-specific medical advice.
faq: At what temperature should kids stay inside?

There is no single cut-off, but when the feels-like temperature passes about 35°C or UV reaches 8 or more, avoid midday outdoor play and move it to early morning or late afternoon, in shade with plenty of water.
Do kids need sunscreen on cloudy days?
Yes. UV passes through cloud, so go by the UV index rather than whether it looks sunny. For babies under six months, prefer shade and covering clothing and ask a doctor before using sunscreen.
Does Lumi Weather warn before rain?
Yes. According to its App Store description, Lumi alerts you before rain and when tomorrow may be rainy, with Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets and a daily reminder at a time you choose.

loc.h1: ฟิลเตอร์วินเทจ: เลือกลุคตามยุค แล้วปรับให้ดูเป็นธรรมชาติ
loc.lead: ฟิลเตอร์วินเทจที่ดูดีไม่ได้แปลว่าใส่ทุกเอฟเฟกต์ให้เต็มที่ รูปส่วนใหญ่ที่ดู “ปลอม” เกิดจากเกรนหนาเกิน ขอบมืดเข้มเกิน และผิวคนกลายเป็นสีส้มหรือเทา

en.title: Vintage Filters by Era: Pick the Look, Keep Photos Natural
en.meta: Pick a vintage filter by era: warm 70s, faded 80s, 90s flash with date stamp, plus how to tune grain, vignette and skin tones so photos don't look muddy.
en.h1: Vintage filters: choose a look by era, then tune it to stay natural
en.lead: A good vintage filter does not mean every effect at full strength. Most photos that look “fake” have too much grain, too dark a vignette and skin that has turned orange or grey.
en.answer: Pick the era first: warm golden 70s tones, faded low-contrast 80s colour, or hard-flash 90s looks with a date stamp. Then lower the filter strength until skin looks like skin, add grain only visible when zoomed, a light vignette, and lift the blacks slightly to grey. The photo reads as real film without looking muddy.
paras: Each vintage era has its own signature. The 70s are warm, with yellow highlights and brown shadows, great for late sun and wooden cafés. The 80s are faded and low in saturation, with shadows that never go fully black, suiting sky and sea shots. The 90s are the compact flash camera: punchy colour, high contrast, often an orange date stamp in the corner, ideal at night and with friends.

The most common failure is skin tone. Strong warm filters turn skin orange; strong faded ones turn it grey. Rather than weakening the whole filter, adjust only the orange range with HSL, lowering saturation a little and raising brightness a touch. Split toning gives warm highlights and cool shadows without shifting the whole image.

Extras such as grain, light leaks, halation and dust work best one or two at a time, not all together. Light leaks suit frames with empty edges; halation shows around light sources at night. If you can preview effects live before pressing the shutter, you can compose for the look while shooting.
look: A wide range of film looks across warm, faded and punchy tones
Separate control of grain, halation, light leaks and vignette
HSL curves and split toning to fix skin tones
Live preview of the look before pressing the shutter
On-device processing with no photo uploads
steps: Read the light and setting, then pick an era: warm for late sun, faded for sea or sky, 90s flash for night.
Apply the filter and lower its strength until skin returns to a natural colour.
Fix the orange range with HSL if skin is still too orange or grey.
Add light grain and a slight vignette; choose either a light leak or halation, not both.
For an old film-print feel, finish with a date stamp or frame.
rows: Matches late sun and wood, but easily turns skin orange
Faded colour, shadows not fully black
Nostalgic mood, but too faded makes skin look grey
Great for night and friends; keep flash from washing faces out
en.fits: PhotoCream Pro: Film Filters suits people who want a vintage look they can fine-tune, not a one-tap filter. It has more than 100 film looks with grain, halation, light leaks and vignette previewed live before the shutter, HSL curves and split toning, skin smoothing that keeps eyes and hair sharp, and text, frames, grain, dust or a date stamp in the style of old film prints. Its Steal the Look feature analyses the colours of a photo you like on device and turns them into an adjustable film tone. Everything is processed on your device.
faq: Is a vintage filter the same as a film filter?
The terms overlap, but film filters usually imitate a specific film stock, while vintage is broader and includes old-camera effects such as light leaks, dust and date stamps.
Why does my face look dull with a vintage filter?
Usually the filter lowers saturation and lifts shadows across the whole image, so skin fades to grey. Lower the filter strength, or brighten just the orange range with HSL instead.
Can I match the colours of a photo I saw online?
PhotoCream Pro has a Steal the Look feature: pick a photo you like and the app analyses its colours on device and turns them into an adjustable film tone for your own photos.

loc.title: ทำแผนเที่ยวรายวันยังไงให้เที่ยวได้จริง ไม่วิ่งรอกทั้งทริป
loc.meta: วิธีทำแผนเที่ยวรายวันให้ใช้ได้จริง: วันละ 3–4 จุด เผื่อเวลาเดินทาง 30% วางจุดใกล้กันไว้วันเดียวกัน และเก็บเที่ยวบิน โรงแรม ตั๋ว ไว้ในวันที่ต้องใช้
loc.h1: แผนเที่ยวรายวัน: สูตรจัดเวลาให้ทริปไม่แน่นจนเหนื่อย
loc.lead: แผนเที่ยวส่วนใหญ่พังตั้งแต่วันแรก ไม่ใช่เพราะเลือกที่เที่ยวผิด แต่เพราะคิดเวลาเดินทาง เวลากิน และเวลารอคิวน้อยเกินไป
loc.answer: แผนเที่ยวที่ใช้ได้จริงควรมีวันละ 3–4 จุดหลัก จัดจุดที่อยู่ใกล้กันไว้วันเดียวกัน เผื่อเวลาเดินทางเพิ่มจากที่แผนที่บอกราว 30% และเว้นช่องว่างอย่างน้อย 30–60 นาทีระหว่างจุด วันแรกที่บินถึงและวันสุดท้ายที่ต้องเช็กเอาต์ให้วางแผนเบาที่สุด แล้วเก็บข้อมูลเที่ยวบิน โรงแรม และตั๋วไว้ในวันที่ต้องใช้จริง
paras: เริ่มจากเวลาที่ล็อกแน่นอนก่อน คือเวลาเครื่องลง เวลาเช็กอินและเช็กเอาต์โรงแรม และรอบตั๋วที่จองไว้ แล้วค่อยเติมสถานที่เที่ยวลงในช่องว่างที่เหลือ วิธีนี้ทำให้เห็นทันทีว่าวันไหนมีเวลาว่างจริงกี่ชั่วโมง ไม่ใช่นับแค่ 9 โมงเช้าถึง 6 โมงเย็นแล้วยัดสถานที่ลงไป

เวลาที่แผนที่บอกคือเวลาขับหรือเดินโดยไม่มีอะไรมาขวาง แต่ทริปจริงมีรถติด หาที่จอด รอรถไฟ และเดินออกจากสถานี การเผื่อเพิ่มราว 30% และจัดสถานที่ตามโซน เช่น วันนี้เมืองเก่า พรุ่งนี้ริมทะเล ช่วยลดเวลานั่งรถไปมาได้มากกว่าการตัดสถานที่ออก

อย่าลืมเวลากินและพัก มื้อกลางวันที่ร้านดังอาจใช้เวลารอคิวเป็นชั่วโมง ถ้ามีเด็กหรือผู้สูงอายุ ช่วงบ่ายควรมีจุดที่ได้นั่งพัก และเช็กสภาพอากาศปลายทางก่อนออกเดินทาง ถ้ามีแนวโน้มฝนตก ให้สลับวันที่เที่ยวในร่มกับกลางแจ้งไว้ล่วงหน้า

en.title: Travel Plan by Day: How to Build One You Can Actually Follow
en.meta: A day-by-day travel plan that works: 3–4 main stops a day, 30% extra travel time, nearby places together, and bookings stored on the day you need them.
en.h1: Day-by-day travel plan: a timing formula that keeps trips from feeling rushed
en.lead: Most travel plans fall apart on day one, not because of the wrong places, but because travel, meal and queue times were underestimated.
en.answer: A workable plan has 3–4 main stops a day, groups nearby places on the same day, adds about 30% to the travel time the map shows and leaves at least 30–60 minutes between stops. Keep arrival day and checkout day as light as possible, and store flight, hotel and ticket details on the day you actually need them.
paras: Start with the fixed times: landing, hotel check-in and checkout, and any booked ticket slots. Then fill the remaining gaps with places. This shows how many free hours each day really has, instead of assuming 9am to 6pm and cramming places in.

Map times assume nothing gets in the way, but real trips have traffic, parking, waiting for trains and walking out of stations. Adding about 30% and grouping places by area, say the old town one day and the coast the next, cuts more back-and-forth than dropping places does.

Remember meals and rest. Lunch at a popular spot can mean an hour in the queue. With children or older travellers, plan somewhere to sit in the afternoon, and check the destination weather before you leave; if rain looks likely, swap indoor and outdoor days ahead of time.
look: Every day of the trip on one timeline, in time order
Clear free time between stops
Flights, hotels, tickets and notes stored on the relevant day
Destination weather before you leave
A quick view of the next stop during the trip without juggling apps
steps: Enter the fixed times first: flights, check-in, checkout and booked ticket slots.
Group places by area and give each area one day, with no more than 3–4 main stops.
Add 30% to travel times and leave 30–60 minutes between stops.
Put meals and rest breaks into the schedule as stops of their own.
Before leaving, check the destination weather and swap indoor and outdoor days if needed.
rows: 3–4 main stops, fewer on travel days
An overpacked plan forces cuts on the spot and tires everyone out
About 30% more than the map says
Traffic, waiting and station walks take longer than expected
Flights, hotels and tickets on the day you use them
No digging through confirmation emails at the counter
en.fits: TripBee Lite: Trip Planner suits people who want a clear day-by-day plan instead of notes scattered across chats and email. It puts every day of the trip on one timeline, from morning flights and transport to sights, hotel check-in and dinner, sorted by time with the free time between stops calculated automatically. Flight, hotel, ticket and note details sit on the relevant day, there is a countdown and destination weather before you leave, and the next stop shows on Apple Watch. No account and no ads.
faq: How many places should a 3-day, 2-night trip cover?
Typically around 8–10 main stops in total: 2–3 on the arrival and departure days and 3–4 on the middle day. In cities with heavy traffic or ferry crossings, plan fewer.
Should I plan every hour?

Schedule fixed items such as flights and ticket slots by the hour, and list other places in order with rough times, checking that the free time between stops is enough. That stays more flexible than locking every minute.
Can I share a TripBee Lite plan with friends?
According to its store description, sharing and inviting friends to edit a trip together via iCloud are part of the one-time Premium purchase in the app.

loc.title: TOEIC lecture : comment répartir les 75 minutes entre les parties 5, 6 et 7
loc.meta: TOEIC Reading : 100 questions en 75 minutes. Environ 10 min pour la partie 5, 8 pour la 6, 55 pour la 7, et un diagnostic pour savoir où vous perdez des points.
loc.h1: TOEIC lecture : un plan de temps pour finir les 100 questions
loc.lead: La plupart des candidats ne perdent pas leurs points de lecture sur des questions trop difficiles, mais sur les dix ou quinze dernières questions de la partie 7, cochées au hasard faute de temps.
loc.answer: La section Reading compte 100 questions en 75 minutes : 30 phrases à compléter (partie 5), 16 questions de textes à trous (partie 6) et 54 questions de compréhension (partie 7). Visez environ 10 minutes pour la partie 5, 8 minutes pour la partie 6 et gardez au moins 55 minutes pour la partie 7, soit à peu près une minute par question sur les textes longs. Si vous ne finissez pas, entraînez d'abord la vitesse de la partie 5, pas la lecture.
paras: La partie 5 est la réserve de temps de toute la section. Une question de grammaire ou de vocabulaire se tranche souvent en 15 à 20 secondes si l'on repère le type (forme du mot, temps, préposition, connecteur) avant de lire les quatre choix. Chaque minute gagnée ici est une minute de plus pour les doubles et triples textes de la partie 7, qui sont les plus longs à traiter.

La partie 6 ressemble à la partie 5, mais une des quatre questions par texte demande d'insérer une phrase entière, ce qui oblige à comprendre le contexte. Lisez le passage d'un trait plutôt que phrase par phrase autour du trou : on répond plus vite et on fait moins d'erreurs de connecteur. Huit minutes pour les quatre textes est un repère réaliste.

En partie 7, lisez d'abord la question, puis cherchez l'information dans le texte au lieu de tout lire en détail. Sur les ensembles à plusieurs documents, une question au moins croise deux textes (une date dans un e-mail, un tarif dans un tableau). Si une question vous bloque plus d'une minute et demie, cochez une réponse, notez-la et passez : il n'y a pas de pénalité pour une mauvaise réponse.
look: Savoir combien de temps vous mettez réellement par question en partie 5, chronomètre en main
Identifier quelle compétence vous coûte le plus de points : grammaire, vocabulaire ou lecture de textes longs
S'entraîner sur des textes longs avec une contrainte de temps, pas seulement sur la justesse
Revoir le vocabulaire des e-mails, factures et annonces, très fréquent en partie 7
Mesurer à nouveau après quelques semaines pour vérifier que le rythme s'est amélioré
steps: Faites un essai chronométré de la section complète et notez l'heure à la fin de chaque partie
Comparez avec le repère 10 / 8 / 55 minutes pour voir où le temps déborde
Si la partie 5 dépasse 12 minutes, travaillez des séries courtes de grammaire chronométrée chaque jour
Si la partie 7 reste inachevée, entraînez la lecture « question d'abord » sur un texte long par jour
Refaites un essai chronométré au bout de trois ou quatre semaines et comparez les temps et la précision
rows: Les questions cochées au hasard à la fin pèsent souvent plus que les erreurs de grammaire
Le type de question repéré avant de lire les choix
C'est la seule partie où l'on peut gagner plusieurs minutes sans perdre en précision
La capacité à retrouver une information sur deux documents
Les ensembles multi-documents représentent une grande part des 54 questions
loc.fits: Aim990 convient si vous préparez la partie lecture du TOEIC et voulez savoir où partent vos points avant de multiplier les exercices. Un diagnostic de 8 minutes désigne vos trois compétences les plus faibles, puis l'application propose chaque jour une seule compétence à travailler, avec de la grammaire chronométrée avec indices de 15 secondes, un entraînement à la gestion du temps sur les textes longs et un journal qui enregistre précision et rythme. L'entraînement quotidien fonctionne hors ligne, sans compte. Les exercices sont originaux et non officiels, et le palier affiché est une estimation, pas un score garanti.
faq: Faut-il commencer la lecture par la partie 7 ?

Certains le font pour sécuriser les textes longs, mais on risque de perdre ensuite des points faciles en partie 5. Pour la plupart des candidats, suivre l'ordre avec un temps limite par partie fonctionne mieux.
Combien de temps par question en partie 7 ?
Environ une minute en moyenne, un peu moins sur les textes simples et un peu plus sur les ensembles de deux ou trois documents.
Deviner une réponse fait-il perdre des points ?
Non, une mauvaise réponse ne retire pas de points. Mieux vaut cocher une réponse à chaque question que laisser des cases vides.

en.title: TOEIC Reading: how to split 75 minutes across Parts 5, 6 and 7
en.meta: TOEIC Reading has 100 questions in 75 minutes. Aim for about 10 minutes on Part 5, 8 on Part 6, 55 on Part 7, and diagnose where your points actually go.
en.h1: TOEIC Reading: a time plan to finish all 100 questions
en.lead: Most test takers do not lose their reading points on hard questions. They lose them on the last ten or fifteen Part 7 questions, guessed in a rush because time ran out.
en.answer: The Reading section has 100 questions in 75 minutes: 30 incomplete sentences (Part 5), 16 text-completion questions (Part 6) and 54 reading-comprehension questions (Part 7). Aim for about 10 minutes on Part 5 and 8 minutes on Part 6, and keep at least 55 minutes for Part 7, roughly one minute per question on the long passages. If you do not finish, train Part 5 speed first, not reading.
paras: Part 5 is the time bank for the whole section. A grammar or vocabulary question can often be settled in 15 to 20 seconds if you spot its type (word form, tense, preposition, connector) before reading the four options. Every minute saved here is an extra minute for the double and triple passages in Part 7, which take the longest.

Part 6 looks like Part 5, but one of the four questions per text asks you to insert a whole sentence, which requires understanding the context. Read the passage in one go instead of sentence by sentence around each gap: it is faster and you make fewer connector mistakes. Eight minutes for the four texts is a realistic target.

In Part 7, read the question first, then scan the text for the answer instead of reading every line. In multi-document sets at least one question links two texts, such as a date in an email and a rate in a table. If a question holds you for more than a minute and a half, mark an answer, note it and move on: a wrong answer carries no penalty.

en.fits: Aim990 suits you if you are preparing for TOEIC Reading and want to know where your points go before piling up more exercises. An 8-minute diagnostic names your three weakest skills, then the app prescribes one skill a day, with timed grammar with 15-second hints, time-management practice on long passages and a log that records accuracy and pace. Daily practice works offline with no account. Exercises are original and unofficial, and the level shown is an estimate, not a guaranteed score.
faq: Should I start Reading with Part 7?
Some people do to secure the long passages, but they then risk losing easy points in Part 5. For most test takers, going in order with a time limit per part works better.
How long per question in Part 7?
About one minute on average, a little less on single short texts and a little more on two- and three-document sets.
Does guessing lose points?
No, a wrong answer does not subtract points. It is better to mark an answer for every question than to leave blanks.

loc.title: Spektrumanalysator auf dem iPhone: FFT, RTA oder Spektrogramm für ein Brummen?
loc.meta: Brummt die Wärmepumpe oder der Kühlschrank? Was FFT, RTA und Spektrogramm zeigen, warum Z-Bewertung bei tiefen Tönen hilft und wo das iPhone-Mikro aufhört.
loc.h1: Spektrumanalysator auf dem iPhone: welche Ansicht für welches Geräusch
loc.lead: Ein einzelner dB-Wert sagt, wie laut es ist, aber nicht, was da brummt. Genau dafür ist ein Spektrumanalysator da: Er zerlegt das Geräusch in Frequenzen und zeigt, ob ein tiefer Ton, ein Pfeifen oder breites Rauschen dahintersteckt.
loc.answer: Für ein gleichmäßiges Brummen nimmst du die FFT-Ansicht: Ein schmaler, hoher Ausschlag zeigt die genaue Frequenz, etwa 50 oder 100 Hz bei Netzbrummen. Die RTA-Ansicht fasst das Signal in Oktavbändern zusammen und passt besser zum Höreindruck. Das Spektrogramm zeigt den zeitlichen Verlauf und verrät Geräusche, die nur zeitweise auftreten, etwa ein Kompressor, der anspringt. Stelle für tiefe Töne die Z- oder C-Bewertung ein, denn die A-Bewertung blendet tiefe Frequenzen stark aus.
paras: FFT, RTA und Spektrogramm messen dasselbe Signal, zeigen es aber unterschiedlich. Die FFT hat eine feine Frequenzauflösung und eignet sich, um einen einzelnen Ton genau zu benennen. Die RTA teilt das Spektrum in Oktavbänder mit logarithmischer Breite, so wie das Ohr Tonhöhen wahrnimmt, und macht Vergleiche zwischen zwei Messungen übersichtlicher. Das Spektrogramm färbt Frequenz und Pegel über die Zeit ein und ist das richtige Werkzeug, wenn das Geräusch kommt und geht.

Die Bewertung ist der häufigste Fehler. Die A-Bewertung bildet die geringere Empfindlichkeit des Ohrs bei tiefen Tönen nach; ein lästiges Brummen um 40 bis 80 Hz erscheint damit deutlich leiser, als es sich anfühlt. Für die Frage „welche Frequenz ist das?“ ist die unbewertete Z-Bewertung die bessere Wahl, die C-Bewertung liegt dazwischen.

Ein eingebautes Smartphone-Mikrofon ist auf Sprache ausgelegt und wird zu sehr tiefen Frequenzen hin unempfindlicher. Für die Suche nach der Ursache, etwa Wärmepumpe, Umwälzpumpe oder Lüftung, reicht das meist aus, weil es um die Lage des Ausschlags geht, nicht um den exakten Pegel. Für belastbare Pegelangaben helfen ein externes Mikrofon und eine Kalibrierung; eine amtliche Beurteilung tieffrequenter Geräusche ersetzt das nicht.

faq: Kann das iPhone 20 Hz zuverlässig messen?

Nur eingeschränkt. Eingebaute Mikrofone werden zu sehr tiefen Frequenzen hin unempfindlicher. Die Frequenz eines Brummens lässt sich oft trotzdem erkennen, der Pegel ist dort aber nur ein Anhaltspunkt.
Warum zeigt die A-Bewertung so wenig, obwohl es deutlich brummt?
Weil die A-Bewertung tiefe Frequenzen stark abschwächt. Für die Analyse tiefer Töne nimm die Z- oder C-Bewertung.
Reicht eine Handymessung für eine Beschwerde?
Als Dokumentation von Zeitpunkt, Frequenz und Verlauf ist sie hilfreich. Für eine rechtlich belastbare Beurteilung ist in der Regel eine Messung mit geeichtem Gerät nötig.

en.title: Spectrum analyzer on iPhone: FFT, RTA or spectrogram for a humming noise?
en.meta: Heat pump or fridge humming? What FFT, RTA and spectrogram views show, why Z weighting helps with low tones, and where an iPhone mic reaches its limits.
en.h1: Spectrum analyzer on iPhone: which view for which noise
en.lead: A single dB reading tells you how loud it is, not what is humming. That is what a spectrum analyzer is for: it splits a sound into frequencies and shows whether a low tone, a whistle or broad noise is behind it.
en.answer: For a steady hum, use the FFT view: a narrow, tall peak shows the exact frequency, such as 50 or 100 Hz for mains hum. The RTA view groups the signal into octave bands and is closer to what you hear. The spectrogram shows the sound over time and reveals noises that only occur now and then, such as a compressor switching on. For low tones choose Z or C weighting, because A weighting strongly suppresses low frequencies.
paras: FFT, RTA and spectrogram measure the same signal but show it differently. FFT has fine frequency resolution and is good for naming a single tone. RTA splits the spectrum into octave bands of logarithmic width, the way the ear perceives pitch, which makes two measurements easier to compare. The spectrogram colours frequency and level over time and is the right tool when the noise comes and goes.

Weighting is the most common mistake. A weighting models the ear's lower sensitivity to low tones, so an annoying hum around 40 to 80 Hz looks much quieter than it feels. To answer "which frequency is this?", unweighted Z weighting is the better choice, with C weighting in between.

A built-in phone microphone is designed for speech and becomes less sensitive towards very low frequencies. For tracking down a cause, such as a heat pump, circulation pump or ventilation, that is usually enough, because what matters is where the peak sits, not its exact level. For reliable level figures, an external microphone and calibration help; they do not replace an official assessment of low-frequency noise.

en.fits: dB Halo suits you if you want to know not only how loud it is but where a noise comes from. FFT spectrum, a real-time analyzer with octave bands and a spectrogram run on the same synchronised timeline without interrupting the measurement. You can choose A, C or Z weighting, use an external microphone, save several calibration profiles and export results as a PDF report or CSV. Processing stays on iPhone and iPad, with no account and no tracking.
faq: Can an iPhone measure 20 Hz reliably?
Only to a limited extent. Built-in microphones lose sensitivity at very low frequencies. The frequency of a hum can often still be identified, but the level there is only a rough guide.
Why does A weighting show so little when the hum is obvious?
Because A weighting strongly attenuates low frequencies. For analysing low tones, use Z or C weighting.
Is a phone measurement enough for a complaint?
It is useful as a record of time, frequency and pattern. A legally robust assessment usually requires a measurement with a calibrated instrument.

loc.title: Bopomofo no Brasil: os 37 símbolos e os tons para famílias que ensinam mandarim
loc.meta: O que é bopomofo (zhuyin), quando escolher em vez do pinyin e como ensinar os 37 símbolos e os tons em casa, em sessões curtas, mesmo morando no Brasil.
loc.h1: Bopomofo para crianças no Brasil: por onde começar em casa
loc.lead: Muitas famílias de origem taiwanesa em São Paulo e em outras cidades querem que os filhos leiam como as crianças de Taiwan. O primeiro passo lá não é o pinyin nem os caracteres: é o bopomofo.
loc.answer: Bopomofo, também chamado zhuyin, é o sistema de 37 símbolos fonéticos usado em Taiwan para ensinar a pronúncia do mandarim antes dos caracteres. São 21 iniciais, 3 mediais e 13 finais, mais as marcas dos quatro tons e do tom neutro. Se a família tem vínculo com Taiwan ou a criança vai usar livros e materiais de lá, comece pelo bopomofo; se o foco é a China continental, o pinyin é o padrão. Em casa, 10 minutos por dia, ouvindo antes de escrever, são suficientes para começar.
paras: A grande vantagem do bopomofo para uma criança brasileira é que os símbolos não se parecem com letras latinas. Com o pinyin, a criança tende a ler "x", "q" ou "zh" como em português e a pronúncia sai errada. Com o bopomofo, cada símbolo é um som novo, sem interferência do alfabeto que ela já está aprendendo na escola.

Os tons são o ponto mais difícil para quem cresce falando português, porque em português a entonação muda a emoção da frase, não o significado da palavra. Em mandarim, mā, má, mǎ e mà são palavras diferentes. Por isso vale treinar o ouvido para os tons desde o começo, com gestos ou imagens que subam, desçam ou façam uma curva, em vez de deixar para depois.

Depois que a criança reconhece os símbolos isolados, o passo seguinte é juntar inicial, medial e final para formar uma sílaba, por exemplo ㄍ + ㄨ + ㄚ. É nessa etapa que a leitura começa de verdade. Revisar todo dia os símbolos que ainda confundem é mais eficiente do que passar rápido por todos os 37.

loc.fits: Lumi Bopomofo serve para famílias que querem começar o bopomofo em casa, na pré-escola ou numa rotina bilíngue, com crianças pequenas. A criança aprende os 37 símbolos de ouvido: ouve um som, escolhe o símbolo certo e dá de comer a um amiguinho. Ela contorna cada símbolo na ordem correta dos traços, anda na montanha-russa dos tons para ouvi-los e junta inicial, medial e final no trem dos sons para formar sílabas. A revisão diária traz de volta os símbolos que ainda não domina. Funciona offline, sem anúncios e sem cadastro.
faq: Bopomofo ou pinyin: qual ensinar primeiro?
Depende do destino da criança. Para quem tem vínculo com Taiwan ou usa materiais de lá, bopomofo primeiro. Para a China continental, o pinyin é o padrão. Muitas crianças aprendem os dois mais tarde.
Com que idade dá para começar?
Muitas famílias começam por volta dos 4 ou 5 anos, com jogos curtos de ouvir e apontar. A escrita dos símbolos pode vir um pouco depois.
Os pais precisam falar mandarim?
Ajuda, mas não é obrigatório para os primeiros passos, desde que a criança ouça a pronúncia correta de cada símbolo e de cada tom.

en.title: Bopomofo in Brazil: the 37 symbols and tones for families teaching Mandarin
en.meta: What bopomofo (zhuyin) is, when to choose it over pinyin, and how to teach the 37 symbols and the tones at home in short sessions, even while living in Brazil.
en.h1: Bopomofo for children in Brazil: where to start at home
en.lead: Many families of Taiwanese origin in São Paulo and other cities want their children to read the way children in Taiwan do. The first step there is neither pinyin nor characters: it is bopomofo.
en.answer: Bopomofo, also called zhuyin, is the system of 37 phonetic symbols used in Taiwan to teach Mandarin pronunciation before characters. There are 21 initials, 3 medials and 13 finals, plus marks for the four tones and the neutral tone. If your family has ties to Taiwan or your child will use books and materials from there, start with bopomofo; if the focus is mainland China, pinyin is the standard. At home, ten minutes a day, listening before writing, is enough to begin.
paras: The big advantage of bopomofo for a Brazilian child is that the symbols do not look like Latin letters. With pinyin, a child tends to read "x", "q" or "zh" the Portuguese way and the pronunciation comes out wrong. With bopomofo, each symbol is a new sound, with no interference from the alphabet they are learning at school.

Tones are the hardest part for children growing up with Portuguese, because in Portuguese intonation changes the emotion of a sentence, not the meaning of a word. In Mandarin, mā, má, mǎ and mà are different words. That is why it pays to train the ear for tones from the start, with gestures or pictures that rise, fall or curve, rather than leaving them for later.

Once the child recognises single symbols, the next step is combining an initial, a medial and a final into a syllable, for example ㄍ + ㄨ + ㄚ. That is where reading really begins. Reviewing every day the symbols that still cause confusion works better than racing through all 37.

en.fits: Lumi Bopomofo suits families who want to start bopomofo with young children at home, in preschool or in a bilingual routine. The child learns the 37 symbols by ear: they hear a sound, pick the right symbol and feed a little friend. They trace each symbol in the correct stroke order, ride the tone roller coaster to hear the tones, and join initial, medial and final on the sound train to build syllables. Daily review brings back the symbols they have not mastered yet. It works offline, with no ads and no sign-up.
faq: Bopomofo or pinyin: which first?
It depends on where the child is headed. For ties to Taiwan or materials from there, bopomofo first. For mainland China, pinyin is the standard. Many children learn both later on.
At what age can we start?
Many families start around four or five with short listen-and-point games. Writing the symbols can come a little later.
Do parents need to speak Mandarin?
It helps but is not required for the first steps, as long as the child hears the correct pronunciation of each symbol and tone.

loc.title: 마지막으로 한 날 기억 안 날 때: 침구·에어컨 필터·엔진오일 날짜 기록법
loc.meta: 이불 빨래, 에어컨 필터 청소, 엔진오일 교체를 마지막으로 한 날이 기억나지 않는다면. 한 날을 바로 기록하고 며칠 지났는지 보는 방법과 주기 정하는 요령.
loc.h1: 마지막으로 한 날, 기억 대신 기록으로 남기는 법
loc.lead: "이불 빨래 언제 했더라?" 하고 사진첩을 뒤지거나 카톡 대화를 검색해 본 적이 있다면, 문제는 기억력이 아니라 기록할 곳이 없다는 데 있습니다.
loc.answer: 마지막으로 한 날을 확실히 알고 싶다면, 일을 끝낸 그 자리에서 날짜를 한 번 기록하고 "며칠 지났는지"로 확인하는 방식이 가장 확실합니다. 미리 날짜를 정해 두는 알림과 달리, 실제로 한 날을 기준으로 다음 시점을 다시 계산하기 때문에 하루이틀 늦어져도 주기가 어긋나지 않습니다. 침구, 에어컨 필터, 엔진오일처럼 "할 때가 됐나?"가 헷갈리는 일부터 시작하세요.
paras: 달력 알림은 "매월 1일 필터 청소"처럼 날짜를 미리 박아 둡니다. 그런데 실제로는 10일에 했다면 다음 알림은 3주 만에 울리고, 깜빡 넘긴 달에는 언제 했는지 기록조차 남지 않습니다. 마지막으로 한 날을 기록해 두면 "23일 지났음"처럼 지금 상태가 바로 보이고, 다음 시점도 실제로 끝낸 날부터 다시 셉니다.

주기는 일마다 다릅니다. 침구는 보통 1~2주에 한 번 세탁을 권하고, 에어컨 필터는 많이 쓰는 여름철에 2주 정도마다 청소하라는 안내가 흔합니다. 엔진오일은 차종과 운전 습관에 따라 크게 달라서, 차량 설명서의 주행거리와 기간 기준을 확인하고 그중 먼저 오는 쪽으로 정하는 것이 안전합니다. 처음에는 넉넉하게 잡고, 몇 번 기록이 쌓이면 실제 간격을 보고 조정하세요.
기록할 대상은 많을수록 좋은 게 아닙니다. 매일 하는 일은 기록하지 않아도 기억나고, 1년에 한 번 하는 일은 일정표에 넣는 편이 낫습니다. 가장 효과가 큰 것은 2주에서 6개월 사이 간격으로 돌아오는 일입니다. 정수기 필터, 화분 분갈이, 반려동물 구충제처럼 "분명 했는데 언제였지?"가 반복되는 항목이 여기에 해당합니다.

먼지가 쌓이면 냉방 효율과 공기 질에 영향을 줍니다
놓치면 정비 비용이 커지고 주행거리만으로는 기간을 놓치기 쉽습니다
loc.fits: Mochi DoneStamp는 "마지막으로 한 날"을 기억이 아니라 기록으로 확인하고 싶은 분께 맞습니다. 다 했으면 한 번 탭해 정확한 시간을 남기고, 마지막으로 한 지 며칠 지났는지 언제든 보여 줍니다. 잘못 누르면 바로 실행 취소할 수 있고, 과거 기록도 추가, 수정, 삭제할 수 있습니다. 분부터 년까지 주기를 정해 두면 때가 됐을 때 알려 주고, 다음 날짜는 실제로 끝낸 날부터 다시 계산됩니다. 대화형 홈 화면 및 잠금 화면 위젯, Siri와 단축어, Apple Watch에서도 마지막 시간을 확인하고 바로 기록할 수 있습니다. 계정과 광고 없이 핵심 데이터는 기기에 보관됩니다.
faq: 캘린더 반복 알림과 뭐가 다른가요?
반복 알림은 정해 둔 날짜에 울릴 뿐 실제로 한 날을 남기지 않습니다. 마지막으로 한 날을 기록하면 며칠 지났는지가 보이고, 다음 시점도 실제로 한 날부터 다시 계산됩니다.
엔진오일 교체 주기는 몇 km로 잡아야 하나요?
차종, 오일 종류, 운전 습관에 따라 다릅니다. 차량 설명서의 주행거리와 기간 기준을 확인하고 먼저 도달하는 쪽에 맞추는 것이 안전합니다.
예전에 한 날짜도 입력할 수 있나요?
네. 과거 기록을 추가하고 수정할 수 있어서, 처음 시작할 때 기억나는 마지막 날짜부터 넣어 두면 됩니다.

en.title: Can't remember the last time you did it? Logging bedding, AC filter and engine oil dates
en.meta: When did you last wash the bedding, clean the AC filter or change the oil? Log the day you did it, see days since at a glance and set sensible intervals.
en.h1: The last time you did it: keep a record instead of relying on memory
en.lead: If you have ever scrolled through your photos or searched old chats to work out when you last washed the duvet, the problem is not your memory. It is that there was nowhere to write it down.
en.answer: If you want to know for sure when you last did something, log the date once, right when you finish, and check it as "days since". Unlike reminders set to fixed dates, this recalculates the next due point from the day you actually did it, so being a day or two late does not throw the cycle off. Start with tasks like bedding, the air-conditioner filter and engine oil, where "is it time yet?" is always unclear.
paras: A calendar reminder fixes the date in advance, such as "clean the filter on the 1st". If you actually did it on the 10th, the next reminder comes after only three weeks, and in a month you skip there is no record at all. Logging the last done date shows your current state straight away, like "23 days ago", and counts the next interval from when you really finished.

Intervals vary by task. Bedding is commonly washed every one to two weeks, and AC filters are often recommended to be cleaned about every two weeks during heavy summer use. Engine oil depends a lot on the car and driving habits, so check the mileage and time limits in your owner's manual and go with whichever comes first. Start generous, then adjust once a few entries show your real spacing.

More items is not better. Daily tasks you will remember anyway, and once-a-year tasks belong in a calendar. The biggest payoff is for things that come round every two weeks to six months: water purifier filters, repotting plants, pet deworming, anything where you keep thinking "I did that, but when?"

steps: Pick just three tasks where you often wonder when you last did them
Enter the last date you remember as a past entry, even if it was not today
Set a rough interval for each; for engine oil, follow the manual
Log each task right where you finish it, every time
After a few entries, look at the real spacing and adjust the intervals
rows: The interval is short so memories blur, and it affects hygiene

en.fits: Mochi DoneStamp suits you if you want to check the last time you did something from a record rather than memory. Tap once when you are done to save the exact time, and it shows how many days have passed whenever you look. You can undo a tap immediately and add, edit or delete past entries. Set an interval from minutes to years and it reminds you when it is due, recalculating the next date from the day you actually finished. Interactive home and lock screen widgets, Siri and Shortcuts, and Apple Watch let you check the last time and log it straight away. No account and no ads; core data stays on your device.
faq: How is this different from a repeating calendar reminder?
A repeating reminder just fires on set dates and does not record when you actually did it. Logging the last done date shows days since and recalculates the next point from the real date.
What mileage should I use for engine oil changes?
It depends on the car, the oil and how you drive. Check the mileage and time limits in your owner's manual and follow whichever you reach first.
Can I enter dates from before I started?
Yes. You can add and edit past entries, so begin by entering the last date you remember for each task.

loc.title: บราวน์นอยส์ ไวท์นอยส์ พิงก์นอยส์ ต่างกันยังไง เลือกแบบไหนดี

loc.h1: บราวน์นอยส์: ฟังตอนไหน ต่างจากไวท์นอยส์อย่างไร
loc.lead: ถ้าเคยเปิดไวท์นอยส์แล้วรู้สึกว่าเสียงซ่าแหลมเกินไปจนนอนไม่หลับ ลองเปลี่ยนเป็นบราวน์นอยส์ เสียงจะทุ้มและนุ่มกว่า คล้ายเสียงน้ำตกไกลๆ หรือฟ้าร้องต่ำๆ ที่ไม่หยุด
loc.answer: บราวน์นอยส์คือเสียงรบกวนที่ความถี่ต่ำดังกว่าความถี่สูง เลยฟังทุ้มและหนักกว่าไวท์นอยส์ (ซ่าเท่ากันทุกความถี่ ฟังแหลม) และพิงก์นอยส์ (อยู่ตรงกลาง คล้ายฝนตกสม่ำเสมอ) บราวน์นอยส์เหมาะกับการกลบเสียงทุ้มอย่างรถวิ่ง มอเตอร์ไซค์ หรือเสียงทีวีห้องข้างๆ และใช้เป็นเสียงพื้นหลังตอนทำงาน ส่วนเรื่องช่วยให้หลับลึกขึ้นนั้นงานวิจัยยังมีจำกัด ให้ลองเองสักหนึ่งสัปดาห์ เปิดเบาที่สุดเท่าที่ยังกลบเสียงรบกวนได้ และตั้งเวลาให้เสียงค่อยๆ เบาลง
paras: ทั้งสามสีต่างกันที่การกระจายพลังงานเสียง ไวท์นอยส์มีพลังงานเท่ากันทุกความถี่ หูคนเราไวต่อเสียงสูงจึงได้ยินเป็นเสียงซ่าแหลม พิงก์นอยส์ลดเสียงสูงลงบางส่วนจนฟังสมดุลขึ้น บราวน์นอยส์ลดเสียงสูงลงมากกว่าอีก จึงเหลือแต่เสียงทุ้มหนา หลายคนบอกว่าฟังได้นานกว่าโดยไม่ล้าหู

การเลือกควรดูจากเสียงที่อยากกลบ เสียงรถบนถนนใหญ่ เสียงคอมเพรสเซอร์แอร์ หรือเสียงเบสจากห้องข้างๆ เป็นเสียงทุ้ม บราวน์นอยส์กลบได้ดีกว่า ส่วนเสียงคนคุยหรือเสียงแหลมเป็นช่วงๆ พิงก์นอยส์หรือการผสมเสียงฝนเข้าไปอาจช่วยได้มากกว่า หลายคนในเมืองไทยที่เปิดพัดลมนอนอยู่แล้ว อาจลองผสมบราวน์นอยส์เบาๆ เข้ากับเสียงพัดลมแทนการเปิดดัง

ความดังสำคัญกว่าสีของเสียง เปิดให้เบาพอที่ยังได้ยินเสียงรอบตัวบ้าง ไม่ควรดังกว่าเสียงฝักบัวเบาๆ และวางลำโพงห่างจากหัวนอน ถ้าใช้กับทารก คำแนะนำทั่วไปคือให้ต่ำกว่าประมาณ 50 เดซิเบลและวางให้ห่างเตียง การให้เสียงค่อยๆ เบาลงหลังหลับแทนการเปิดทั้งคืนก็ช่วยลดการได้ยินเสียงต่อเนื่องนานเกินไป

en.title: Brown noise vs white and pink noise: which one should you pick?
en.meta: Brown noise is deeper than white or pink noise and suits masking traffic or condo neighbours. How to choose, set a sensible volume and use a fade-out timer.
en.h1: Brown noise: when to use it and how it differs from white noise
en.lead: If white noise has ever felt too hissy to fall asleep to, try brown noise. It is deeper and softer, like a distant waterfall or a low, unbroken rumble of thunder.
en.answer: Brown noise is noise where low frequencies are louder than high ones, so it sounds deeper and heavier than white noise (equal energy at every frequency, heard as a sharp hiss) and pink noise (in between, like steady rain). Brown noise is good for masking low sounds such as traffic, motorbikes or a neighbour's TV, and as background sound for work. Evidence that it deepens sleep is still limited, so try it yourself for a week, play it as quietly as still masks the disturbance, and set a timer that fades it out.
paras: The three colours differ in how sound energy is spread. White noise has equal energy at every frequency, and because our ears are sensitive to highs, it sounds like a sharp hiss. Pink noise reduces the highs somewhat so it sounds more balanced. Brown noise reduces them further, leaving a thick, low sound that many people find they can listen to longer without ear fatigue.

Choose by the sound you want to cover. Traffic on a main road, an air-conditioner compressor or bass from next door are low sounds that brown noise masks better. For voices or intermittent high sounds, pink noise or mixing in rain may work better. Many people in Thailand who already sleep with a fan on can try adding quiet brown noise to the fan sound instead of turning anything up.

Volume matters more than colour. Keep it low enough that you can still hear your surroundings a little, no louder than a gentle shower, and place the speaker away from your pillow. For babies, common guidance is to stay below about 50 decibels and keep the device away from the cot. Letting the sound fade after you fall asleep, rather than playing it all night, also limits continuous exposure.

en.fits: Sereno suits you if you want to compare brown noise with white and pink noise, then mix it with rain, ocean waves, a campfire or a fan, adjusting each layer's volume, balance and EQ into your own mix. Colour noises are generated in real time on the device, while nature sounds are real field recordings reordered at random. There are ready-made scenes for focus and deep sleep, and a sleep timer that gradually lowers the volume. It plays in the background, can be controlled from the lock screen and works offline, with no ads and no account.
faq: Does brown noise really deepen sleep?
Research on this is still limited. What is clearer is that a steady sound helps mask noises that wake you. Try it for a week in a row and observe how you sleep.
Can I play it all night?
Yes, if it is quiet, but many people set a timer to fade out after they fall asleep so they are not exposed to continuous sound all night.
Is it OK for a young child?
Yes, but keep it quiet, below about 50 decibels, and place the device away from the child's bed.

loc.title: Corrigir foto borrada: tremida, fora de foco ou comprimida pelo WhatsApp?
loc.meta: Antes de corrigir uma foto borrada, descubra o tipo de borrão: tremida, fora de foco, ruído de pouca luz ou compressão do WhatsApp. Cada um pede outro ajuste.
loc.h1: Corrigir foto borrada no celular: identifique o borrão antes de editar
loc.lead: Nem toda foto borrada é igual. Uma foto tremida, uma desfocada e uma que chegou embaçada pelo WhatsApp parecem parecidas na tela, mas cada uma tem uma causa e uma correção diferentes.
loc.answer: Primeiro veja de onde veio a foto. Se ela chegou pelo WhatsApp, peça o arquivo original (enviado como documento ou em HD), porque a compressão apaga detalhes que nenhuma edição devolve por completo. Depois identifique o borrão: rastros na mesma direção indicam tremida, contornos macios por igual indicam foco errado, e granulação colorida indica ruído de pouca luz. Borrões leves e moderados costumam melhorar bem com nitidez, redução de ruído ou super-resolução; um rosto que está só alguns pixels numa foto muito tremida não volta a ser exato, e a ferramenta reconstrói detalhes em vez de recuperar os originais.
paras: O WhatsApp reduz a resolução e comprime as fotos para enviar mais rápido. Em fotos de família, festas e formaturas, que circulam muito por grupos, isso é a causa mais comum de "foto embaçada". O ideal é corrigir a partir da maior versão disponível: o original no celular de quem tirou, ou o arquivo reenviado como documento. Corrigir uma cópia de uma cópia multiplica os artefatos.

Tremida e desfoque pedem tratamentos diferentes. Na foto tremida, os contornos aparecem duplicados ou arrastados numa direção, e a nitidez focada nesse tipo de borrão ajuda mais. Na foto fora de foco, o fundo pode estar nítido e o rosto macio; aí o ganho é menor e depende de quanto detalhe ainda existe. Em fotos noturnas, o problema geralmente é ruído, e aplicar só nitidez deixa a granulação mais forte: reduza o ruído primeiro.

Ferramentas com IA de super-resolução geram detalhes plausíveis a partir do que existe na imagem. Isso é ótimo para deixar uma foto apresentável, mas não serve como prova de quem está na imagem nem para ler uma placa ilegível. Compare sempre antes e depois em tamanho real e desconfie de resultados com pele lisa demais ou texto que "aparece" onde antes não havia nada.

loc.fits: Unblurry serve para quem quer corrigir fotos tremidas, suaves ou fora de foco direto no iPhone, sem enviar nada para a nuvem e sem conta. Ele tem oito modos: Auto Clear para borrões do dia a dia, Nitidez para foco suave e tremidas, Remover ruído para granulação de ISO alto, Pouca luz para fotos escuras, Documento para textos e quadros, Super-resolução com IA, Ampliação 4× e Retrato e restauração para rostos e fotos antigas. Pressionar a imagem mostra o original para comparar antes e depois. Sem anúncios e sem rastreamento.
faq: Dá para recuperar uma foto muito tremida?
Borrões leves e moderados melhoram bastante. Em fotos muito tremidas, a imagem fica mais apresentável, mas detalhes finos como letras pequenas ou feições exatas podem não voltar.
Por que a foto ficou borrada depois que mandei pelo WhatsApp?
O WhatsApp comprime as fotos e reduz a resolução. Para manter a qualidade, envie como documento ou use a opção de qualidade HD.
A minha foto é enviada para algum servidor?

en.title: Fix a blurry photo: camera shake, missed focus or WhatsApp compression?
en.meta: Before fixing a blurry photo, work out the type of blur: shake, missed focus, low-light noise or WhatsApp compression. Each one needs a different fix.
en.h1: Fix a blurry photo on your phone: identify the blur before you edit
en.lead: Not every blurry photo is the same. A shaky shot, an out-of-focus one and one that arrived soft via WhatsApp look alike on screen, but each has a different cause and a different fix.
en.answer: First check where the photo came from. If it arrived via WhatsApp, ask for the original file (sent as a document or in HD), because compression removes detail no edit fully brings back. Then identify the blur: streaks in one direction mean camera shake, evenly soft edges mean missed focus, and coloured grain means low-light noise. Mild and moderate blur usually improves well with sharpening, noise removal or super-resolution; a face that is only a few pixels in a badly shaken photo will not become exact again, and the tool reconstructs detail rather than recovering the original.
paras: WhatsApp reduces resolution and compresses photos to send them faster. For family, party and graduation photos that circulate through group chats, this is the most common cause of a "blurry photo". It is best to fix the largest version available: the original on the phone of whoever took it, or the file resent as a document. Fixing a copy of a copy multiplies the artefacts.

Shake and missed focus need different treatment. In a shaky photo, edges look doubled or dragged in one direction, and sharpening aimed at that kind of blur helps most. In an out-of-focus photo the background may be sharp while the face is soft; the gain is smaller there and depends on how much detail still exists. In night shots the problem is usually noise, and sharpening alone makes the grain worse: reduce noise first.

AI super-resolution tools generate plausible detail from what is in the image. That is great for making a photo presentable, but not as proof of who is in it or for reading an illegible number plate. Always compare before and after at full size, and be suspicious of overly smooth skin or text that "appears" where there was nothing before.

It has eight modes: Auto Clear for everyday blur, Sharpen for soft focus and shake, Denoise for high-ISO grain, Low Light for dark photos, Document for text and whiteboards, AI Super-Resolution, 4x Upscale, and Portrait and Restore for faces and old photos. faq: Can a very shaky photo be recovered?
Mild and moderate blur improves a lot. In very shaky photos the image becomes more presentable, but fine details like small text or exact facial features may not come back.
Why did my photo get blurry after sending it on WhatsApp?
WhatsApp compresses photos and lowers the resolution. To keep quality, send it as a document or use the HD quality option.

With Unblurry, processing happens on the device and photos never leave your phone.

loc.title: iPhone 電池檢測怎麼做？最大容量、循環次數與換電池時機
loc.meta: iPhone 電池檢測先看「設定 › 電池」的最大容量，再看循環次數與發燙、掉電速度。低於 80% 或出現維修提示再考慮換。買賣二手機也照這套看。
loc.h1: iPhone 電池檢測：三個數字看懂電池還能不能用
loc.lead: 很多人搜電池檢測，其實想知道的是「該不該換電池」或「這台二手機電池好不好」。只看一個百分比不夠，最大容量、循環次數和平常的耗電、發燙要一起看。
loc.answer: 到「設定 › 電池 › 電池健康度與充電」看最大容量：80% 以上通常還堪用；低於 80%，或頁面出現「維修」提示，就是考慮更換的時機。iPhone 15 以後的機型可在「設定 › 一般 › 關於本機」看到循環次數。接著觀察一週的每小時耗電與發燙時段，若容量還高卻掉電很快，問題多半在使用習慣或某個 App，不一定是電池老化。
paras: 最大容量是電池現在能存的電量和全新時相比的比例。蘋果的說法是：一般 iPhone 電池在正常狀況下約 500 次完整充電循環後仍保有約 80% 原始容量，iPhone 15 系列起提高到約 1,000 次。所以兩年的手機掉到 85% 很常見，不代表壞了；真正要注意的是低於 80%，或系統顯示效能管理已啟用、出現維修建議。
單看百分比會漏掉兩件事。第一是趨勢：同樣 86%，一台半年掉 1%、另一台一個月掉 2%，狀況完全不同，要隔一段時間記錄才看得出來。第二是熱：長時間高溫是電池老化最快的原因之一，邊充電邊玩遊戲、放在車上曝曬，都比充電次數更傷。系統只告訴你整台手機的熱狀態，不是電池本身溫度，所以要看的是「常在什麼時段發燙」。
買賣二手 iPhone 時，電池是最常被問、也最容易說不清楚的一項。賣方截一張最大容量的圖，買方不知道是不是這台、什麼時候截的。比較好的做法是當面打開設定核對，再附上一份寫明數值來源、測量日期的整理，雙方都安心。
look: 最大容量：80% 是大多數人決定換電池的分界線，不是唯一標準
循環次數：iPhone 15 以後可直接在設定看到，舊機型要從系統分析資料取得
趨勢比單一數字重要：同一個百分比，掉得快和掉得慢意義不同
發燙時段：常在充電或某些時段發熱，比充電次數更值得改
數值來源要寫清楚：哪些是系統顯示、哪些是自己輸入或推估
steps: 打開「設定 › 電池 › 電池健康度與充電」，記下最大容量與有沒有維修提示
iPhone 15 以後到「設定 › 一般 › 關於本機」記下循環次數；舊機型可從「分析資料」檔取得

調整充電習慣：避免邊充邊重度使用，合適時把上限設在 80–90%

loc.fits: BattAI 適合想把電池檢測整理成看得懂結果的人：它把你在「設定 › 電池」看到的最大容量轉成 0–100 的健康分數，逐項列出容量、循環次數、使用年限、熱暴露、充電習慣的扣分原因；平常持續記錄每小時耗電、近 7 天熱狀態和每次充電的保養分數，讀值相隔 30 天後顯示每月容量變化。要賣舊機時，可匯出一頁二手轉讓報告（PDF 或 PNG），逐項標示數值來源。要注意的是，BattAI 讀不到最大容量，需要你自己輸入或從分析資料檔匯入；分數是參考值，不是原廠數據。
faq: 電池最大容量 85% 需要換嗎？
通常不需要。80% 以上多半還能正常使用一天；比起數字本身，更該看它掉得快不快、手機是否常發燙，以及設定裡有沒有出現維修提示。
有沒有 App 能直接讀出 iPhone 的最大容量？
系統沒有開放這個數值給第三方 App。檢測類 App 能自己記錄的是電量、充電狀態與整台手機的熱狀態，最大容量與循環次數要由你從設定輸入，或從系統分析資料檔匯入。
充電充到 100% 會比較傷電池嗎？
長時間停在 100% 加上高溫，會加快老化。若生活作息允許，把充電上限設在 80–90%、避免邊充電邊玩遊戲，是最簡單的保養方式。

en.title: How to check iPhone battery health: capacity, cycles, and when to replace
en.meta: Start with Maximum Capacity in Settings > Battery, then check cycle count, drain per hour and heat. Below 80% or a service notice means it is time to replace.
en.h1: iPhone battery check: three numbers that tell you if the battery is still fine
en.lead: Most people checking their battery really want to know one thing: replace it or not, or whether a used iPhone is a good buy. One percentage is not enough. Capacity, cycles and everyday drain and heat belong together.
en.answer: Open Settings > Battery > Battery Health & Charging and read Maximum Capacity. Above 80% is usually still fine; below 80%, or a Service message, is the point to consider a replacement. On iPhone 15 and later the cycle count is in Settings > General > About. Then watch a week of hourly drain and heat: if capacity is high but the phone still dies fast, the cause is usually usage or an app, not battery wear.
paras: Maximum Capacity compares what the battery can hold now with when it was new. Apple says a typical iPhone battery keeps about 80% of its original capacity after around 500 full cycles under normal conditions, and iPhone 15 models raise that to about 1,000. So a two-year-old phone at 85% is normal. What matters is dropping below 80%, performance management being applied, or a service recommendation.

A single percentage hides two things. One is the trend: two phones at 86% are very different if one lost 1% in six months and the other lost 2% in a month, and you only see that by recording over time. The other is heat: long periods of high temperature age a battery faster than charge count, such as gaming while charging or leaving the phone in a hot car. The system only reports the thermal state of the whole phone, not the battery temperature, so the useful question is when it tends to run hot.

When buying or selling a used iPhone, the battery is the most asked and least clearly answered item. A screenshot of the capacity screen does not prove which phone it came from or when. Checking Settings together in person, plus a summary that states each value's source and date, is fairer to both sides.
look: Maximum Capacity: 80% is the line most people use to decide on a replacement, not the only signal
Cycle count: shown in Settings on iPhone 15 and later; older models need the system analytics data
Trend over a single number: the same percentage means different things if it falls fast or slowly
Heat periods: running hot while charging or at certain times is worth fixing before anything else
Clear sources: know which values come from the system and which were typed in or estimated
steps: Open Settings > Battery > Battery Health & Charging and note Maximum Capacity and any service message
On iPhone 15 and later note the cycle count in Settings > General > About; older models can get it from an analytics file
Watch hourly drain and heat for a week to find when the battery falls fastest
Adjust charging habits: avoid heavy use while charging and cap charging at 80–90% when it suits you
Check Maximum Capacity again after 30 days or more and judge by how much it changed
rows: Is Maximum Capacity below 80%, is there a service message
That is the practical line Apple and most repair advice use
High capacity with fast drain usually points to usage or an app
Check capacity in Settings in person, with sources and a date
A screenshot cannot show which phone it is or when it was taken
en.fits: BattAI fits people who want a battery check they can actually read. It turns the Maximum Capacity you see in Settings > Battery into a 0–100 health score and lists what lowers it: capacity, cycle count, device age, heat exposure and charging habits. It keeps recording hourly drain, the last 7 days of thermal state and a care score for each charge, and once readings are at least 30 days apart it shows monthly capacity change. Before selling, you can export a one-page resale report as PDF or PNG with the source of each value. Note that BattAI cannot read Maximum Capacity itself; you type it in or import it from an analytics file, and scores are estimates, not official values.
faq: Should I replace a battery at 85% capacity?
Usually not. Above 80% most phones still last a normal day. More important than the number is how fast it falls, whether the phone often runs hot, and whether Settings shows a service message.
Can an app read my iPhone's Maximum Capacity directly?

No. iOS does not expose that value to third-party apps. Battery apps can record charge level, charging state and the phone's thermal state; capacity and cycle count come from your input or an imported analytics file.
Is charging to 100% bad for the battery?
Sitting at 100% for long periods, especially when warm, speeds up aging. If your routine allows, capping charging at 80–90% and not gaming while charging are the easiest habits to change.

loc.title: 유아 수학 놀이, 문제집보다 먼저 해야 할 수 감각 놀이 방법
loc.meta: 유아 수학 놀이는 하루 10분, 세기·모으기·비교부터. 손가락·주사위·수직선처럼 눈에 보이는 그림으로 시작하고, 틀려도 혼내지 않는 것이 핵심입니다.
loc.h1: 유아 수학 놀이: 연산 문제집 전에 집에서 하는 수 감각 놀이
loc.lead: "우리 아이 수학, 언제부터 뭘 해야 하지?" 하고 수학 놀이를 찾는 부모님이 많습니다. 정답은 계산 속도가 아니라 수 감각입니다. 숫자를 보고 양을 떠올릴 수 있어야 덧셈도 구구단도 무너지지 않습니다.
loc.answer: 만 3~5세는 하루 10분이면 충분합니다. 순서는 ① 하나씩 짚으며 세기 ② 두 묶음을 모으기·가르기 ③ 많다·적다 비교하기 ④ 규칙 찾기입니다. 주사위 눈, 손가락, 십틀(10칸 판)처럼 양이 눈에 보이는 도구를 쓰고, 틀렸을 때 바로 정답을 말해 주기보다 "다시 세어 볼까?"로 아이가 스스로 찾게 하세요. 받아올림이나 구구단은 이 감각이 생긴 뒤에 들어가야 오래갑니다.
paras: 수학 놀이에서 가장 흔한 실수는 숫자 읽기와 세기를 같은 것으로 보는 것입니다. 1부터 20까지 줄줄 외우는 아이도 사탕 7개를 하나씩 짚어 세라고 하면 중간에 건너뛰거나 두 번 세곤 합니다. 하나에 한 번씩 짚기, 마지막에 센 수가 전체 개수라는 것, 이 두 가지가 먼저입니다. 계단 오를 때, 장난감 정리할 때처럼 생활 속에서 세는 기회를 자주 만드는 것이 문제집보다 효과적입니다.

다음 단계는 "5와 3을 모으면 8"처럼 수를 쪼개고 합치는 감각입니다. 십틀이나 주사위 눈처럼 칸과 점으로 보면, 아이는 8을 하나씩 세지 않고 "5하고 3"으로 한눈에 봅니다. 이것이 나중에 받아올림 있는 덧셈(8+5를 8+2+3으로 바꾸기)의 바탕이 됩니다. 우리나라 교육과정에서도 1학년에 모으기·가르기와 받아올림을, 2학년에 곱셈구구를 배우니, 유아기에는 앞부분을 놀이로 충분히 다지는 게 좋습니다.
마지막으로 분위기입니다. 틀릴 때마다 지적을 받으면 아이는 수학을 "틀리면 혼나는 것"으로 기억합니다. 짧게 끝내고, 맞힌 순간을 함께 기뻐해 주고, 아이가 "한 번 더"를 말할 때 멈추는 편이 다음 날도 하고 싶게 만듭니다. 글을 아직 못 읽는 아이라면 문제를 소리 내어 읽어 주고 그림으로 보여 주는 방식이어야 혼자서도 참여할 수 있습니다.
