faq: 수학 놀이는 몇 살부터 시작하나요?
만 3세 전후로 생활 속 세기부터 시작하면 됩니다. 연산 문제집은 하나씩 정확히 세고, 5와 10을 기준으로 수를 모으고 가를 수 있게 된 뒤가 좋습니다.
앱으로 하는 수학 놀이, 화면 시간이 걱정돼요.
하루 10분 정도로 정해 두고, 앱에서 한 놀이를 블록이나 손가락으로 다시 해 보게 하면 화면 밖 경험과 연결됩니다. 짧게 끝내는 것이 습관 만들기에도 유리합니다.
구구단은 언제 외우게 해야 하나요?
교육과정상 곱셈구구는 2학년에서 배웁니다. 그 전에 "2씩, 5씩 뛰어 세기"를 놀이로 해 두면 외우는 부담이 크게 줄어듭니다.

en.title: Math play for young kids: number-sense games before worksheets
en.meta: Math play for ages 3–5 works best at 10 minutes a day: counting, combining, comparing and patterns, with dice, fingers and ten-frames, and no scolding.
en.h1: Math play for preschoolers: number-sense games to do before drill books
en.lead: Parents searching for math play usually want to know where to start. The answer is number sense, not speed. A child who can picture the quantity behind a number keeps up later with addition and times tables.
en.answer: For ages 3 to 5, ten minutes a day is enough. Go in this order: count objects one by one, combine and split two groups, compare more and fewer, then find patterns. Use tools that show quantity, such as dice, fingers and a ten-frame, and when a child gets it wrong, ask them to count again rather than giving the answer. Carrying and times tables stick better once this sense is in place.
paras: The most common mistake is treating reciting numbers as counting. A child who can say 1 to 20 may still skip or double-count when touching seven sweets. Touching each item once, and knowing the last number said is the total, come first. Everyday chances to count, such as stairs or tidying toys, do more than a workbook.

Next comes splitting and combining: 5 and 3 make 8. On a ten-frame or dice, a child sees 8 as 5 and 3 at a glance instead of counting one by one. That is the base for addition with carrying later, turning 8 + 5 into 8 + 2 + 3. In the Korean curriculum, combining and splitting and carrying come in grade 1 and multiplication tables in grade 2, so the preschool years are best spent on the early part through play.

Finally, mood. If every mistake gets corrected sharply, children remember math as the thing they get told off for. Keep sessions short, celebrate the right answers together, and stop while they still want one more. For children who cannot read yet, problems need to be read aloud and shown as pictures so they can take part on their own.
look: Visible quantity: dice, ten-frames and number lines that show numbers as pictures
No reading needed: problems are read aloud and understandable from pictures alone
Reaction to mistakes: encourages another try instead of harsh sounds or penalties
A clear progression: from counting to addition and subtraction, then clocks and money
Parent view: shows which area is weak so you can practise just that
steps: Count in daily life: stairs, blocks or fruit, touching each one, then ask how many in total
Combine and split: use fingers or a ten-frame and see numbers as five and some more
Mix in comparing and patterns: more or fewer, and what comes after red, blue, red
Fix ten minutes a day at the same time and stop while it is still fun
Once a week, check which problem types keep stopping your child and play those again
rows: Counts one by one and knows the last number is the total
Reciting is not the same as understanding quantity, which every later skill needs
Can picture combining and splitting 10 without objects
Grade 1 addition with carrying relies on making ten
Whether mistakes feel like being told off
Negative memories wear down confidence before ability
en.fits: Lumi Math Planet suits families who want picture-based math play for children who cannot read yet through the early school years. It reads each of its 46 problem types aloud and shows them with dice, ten-frames, number lines and bar graphs, stepping up automatically from counting, addition and subtraction to times tables, clocks, money, patterns and logic. A right answer lights up a small planet, and a wrong one gets encouragement with no harsh beep. Parents see progress across five areas, can focus practice on weak spots, and can print worksheets with answer keys or save them as PDF. There are no ads and no account.
faq: What age should math play start?
Around age 3, with counting in daily life. Drill books fit better once a child counts accurately and can combine and split numbers around 5 and 10.
I worry about screen time with math apps.
Set about ten minutes a day and have your child redo what they played with blocks or fingers afterwards. Short sessions also help the habit last.
When should kids memorise times tables?
In the Korean curriculum multiplication tables come in grade 2. Skip-counting by 2s and 5s as a game beforehand makes memorising much easier.

loc.title: 副業記帳怎麼記？每個案子分開算，才看得出哪個真的有賺
loc.meta: 副業記帳的重點是和生活開銷分開、每個案子各算淨額。收入記實收與扣繳，支出記設備、材料、平台抽成，年底報稅與二代健保補充保費才對得上。
loc.h1: 副業記帳：一個案子一本帳，收入減支出才是真的賺多少
loc.lead: 接了接案、團購、市集和家教，月底存款好像變多了，卻說不出哪一個副業真的有賺。問題通常不是記得不夠多，而是全部混在同一本帳裡。
loc.answer: 副業記帳只要做到三件事：①副業和日常開銷分開記；②每個副業或每個案子各自一本帳，收入減掉專屬支出就是它的淨額；③收入記「實際入帳」並另記被扣掉的稅與二代健保補充保費，支出記設備、材料、平台抽成與交通。這樣每個月一眼看出哪個案子值得做，年底報稅時也對得上扣繳憑單。
paras: 很多人副業記帳記到一半放棄，是因為把它當成生活記帳的延伸，結果午餐、房租和買給客戶的材料混在一起，最後算出來的「副業收入」根本沒扣成本。先切開：副業的錢只記副業相關的收支。如果同時有兩三個副業，再各自切開，因為接案設計和週末市集的成本結構完全不同，混在一起就看不出哪一個在拖後腿。
收入要記清楚「入帳金額」和「被扣掉的部分」。在台灣，單次給付達一定金額時，給付方常會先扣繳所得稅，部分所得類別還會扣二代健保補充保費（費率 2.11%），實際入帳比報價少。把報價、扣繳和實收分開記，年初收到扣繳憑單時才能核對，也不會高估自己的收入。實際扣繳門檻與所得類別以國稅局、健保署公告為準。
支出則要記「為這個副業才花的錢」：設備、軟體、材料、運費、平台手續費、交通。有些成本是跨案子共用的，例如同一台相機拍了好幾個案子，這時用標籤標出設備或客戶，再跨案子加總，就能知道一台設備總共撐起多少收入。月底只看兩個數字：每個副業的淨額，以及每小時大概賺多少。
look: 能不能分開記：每個副業或案子有自己的帳本與淨額
能不能跨案子看：同一個客戶、同一台設備在不同案子的收支合計
幣別：接海外案子時，每個案子能不能用自己的幣別與匯率
記帳要快：在手機、手錶或小工具上隨手記一筆，才不會月底補記
能不能匯出：報稅、對帳或給會計時能匯出 CSV、PDF
steps: 列出所有副業，每一個建一本帳，不和日常生活開銷混記
每筆收入記報價、被扣的稅與補充保費、實際入帳三個數字
每筆支出只記為這個副業花的錢，並用標籤標出客戶或設備
每個月底看每個副業的淨額，搭配大概花的時數估每小時收入
年初收到扣繳憑單時，用帳本的扣繳紀錄逐筆核對，再匯出備份
rows: 每個副業是否各自算淨額
混在一起看不出哪個在賺、哪個在賠
每個案子的幣別與當時匯率
匯率變動會讓實際收入和報價差很多
扣繳金額與實收是否分開記
才能核對扣繳憑單，避免漏報或高估收入
loc.fits: MoneyTag 適合同時經營好幾個副業或案子、想各自算清楚的人：每個專案就是一本獨立的帳，有自己的交易與幣別，收入減支出直接顯示這個專案的淨額。任何一筆收支都能貼標籤，標籤頁把同一個標籤在所有專案裡的收入、支出與淨額合計起來，適合用來追蹤客戶或設備。外幣案子可用約每 6 小時更新的公開匯率或手動匯率換算。iPhone 與 iPad 同一本帳，也能在 Apple Watch 或主畫面、鎖定畫面小工具上看狀態、隨手記一筆，並匯出 CSV、PDF 或相片、備份與還原。
faq: 副業記帳和生活記帳可以放在同一個 App 嗎？
可以，但要分成不同的帳本或專案。重點是副業的收支不能和午餐、房租混在一起，否則算不出副業的真實淨額。
副業收入被扣了稅和二代健保，要記多少？
建議三個數字都記：報價、被扣繳的金額、實際入帳。這樣年初對扣繳憑單最快。哪些所得會被扣、門檻多少，以國稅局與健保署公告為準。
設備是好幾個案子共用的，成本要記在哪裡？
可以記在主要使用的那個案子，再用同一個設備標籤標出相關收支，跨案子加總就能看出這台設備總共帶來多少收入。

en.title: Side hustle bookkeeping: one ledger per gig to see what really pays
en.meta: Keep side hustle money apart from daily spending and give each gig its own ledger. Record payouts with withholding, and costs like gear, materials and fees.
en.h1: Side hustle bookkeeping: one ledger per gig, income minus costs
en.lead: Freelance jobs, group buys, weekend markets and tutoring can make your balance grow while you still cannot say which one actually makes money. The usual problem is not tracking too little, it is tracking everything in one place.
en.answer: Side hustle bookkeeping needs three things: keep it separate from everyday spending; give each side hustle or project its own ledger so income minus its own costs is its net; and record income as the amount actually received, with any withheld tax or health insurance premium noted, and costs as gear, materials, platform fees and travel. Each month you see which gig is worth it, and tax time matches your withholding statements.
paras: Many people give up because they treat side income as part of personal budgeting, so lunch, rent and client materials end up mixed and the side income never has its costs taken out. Split it first: side hustle money only records side hustle income and costs. With two or three side hustles, split again, because design freelancing and a weekend market stall have completely different costs.

Record both the payout and what was taken out of it. In Taiwan, payers often withhold income tax on larger single payments, and some income types also have the NHI supplementary premium (2.11%) deducted, so what arrives is less than the quote. Recording quote, withholding and amount received separately lets you check withholding statements later and keeps you from overstating income. Exact thresholds and income types follow the tax bureau and NHI announcements.

For costs, record only what you spent for that side hustle: equipment, software, materials, shipping, platform fees, travel. Some costs are shared, such as one camera used for several jobs; tag the gear or client and total across projects to see how much income that equipment supports. At month end, look at two numbers: each side hustle's net, and roughly what it earns per hour.
look: Separate books: each side hustle or project has its own ledger and net
Cross-project view: totals for the same client or the same equipment across jobs
Currency: each project can use its own currency and exchange rate for overseas work
Fast entry: log on the phone, watch or widget so nothing waits until month end
Export: CSV or PDF for taxes, reconciliation or your accountant
steps: List every side hustle and give each its own ledger, separate from daily spending
For each payment, record the quote, withheld tax and premium, and the amount received
Record only costs spent for that side hustle, tagged by client or equipment
At month end, check each side hustle's net and estimate income per hour
When withholding statements arrive, check them line by line against your ledger, then export a backup
rows: Does each one show its own net
Mixed together you cannot tell which earns and which loses
Each project's currency and the rate at the time
Exchange rates can move income far from the quote
Withholding and amount received recorded separately
Lets you match statements and avoid under- or over-reporting
en.fits: MoneyTag fits people running several side hustles or projects who want each one counted on its own. Every project is a separate ledger with its own transactions and currency, and income minus expenses shows that project's net. Any entry can carry tags, and the Tags view totals income, expenses and net for one tag across all projects, which works well for clients or equipment. Foreign-currency work can use public rates refreshed about every 6 hours or a manual rate. iPhone and iPad share one book, Apple Watch and Home and Lock Screen widgets show status and take quick entries, and you can export CSV, PDF or photos and back up and restore.
faq: Can side hustle and personal budgeting share one app?
Yes, as long as they are separate ledgers or projects. Side income and costs must not mix with lunch and rent, or the real net disappears.
Tax and the NHI premium were deducted. What should I record?
All three numbers: the quote, the amount withheld and the amount received. That makes checking withholding statements quick. Which income is withheld and the thresholds follow official announcements.
Where do I put equipment shared by several jobs?
Record it under the project that uses it most, and tag related entries with the same equipment tag; totals across projects show how much income that equipment brings in.

term: รูปติดบัตร ฟรี

loc.title: ทำรูปติดบัตรเองที่บ้าน ถ่ายยังไง ขนาดไหน พิมพ์ที่ไหนให้ประหยัด
loc.meta: ทำรูปติดบัตรเองได้ด้วยมือถือ ถ่ายหน้าตรงชิดผนังสีเรียบ ใช้แสงธรรมชาติ ครอปให้ตรงขนาดที่หน่วยงานกำหนด แล้วจัดหลายรูปลงกระดาษ 4×6 นิ้วแผ่นเดียวไปพิมพ์
loc.h1: รูปติดบัตรทำเองได้: ถ่าย ครอป และพิมพ์ให้ตรงขนาดที่ต้องใช้
loc.lead: คนที่ค้นหารูปติดบัตรฟรีส่วนใหญ่ต้องการรูปด่วนสำหรับสมัครงาน สมัครเรียน หรือยื่นเอกสาร และไม่อยากเสียเวลาไปร้านถ่ายรูป ข่าวดีคือทำเองได้ ถ้ารู้ว่าต้องเช็กอะไรบ้าง
loc.answer: ทำเองได้ใน 3 ขั้น: ① ถ่ายหน้าตรงด้วยมือถือ ยืนห่างผนังสีพื้นเรียบราวครึ่งเมตร หันหน้าเข้าหาหน้าต่างให้แสงเท่ากันทั้งหน้า ② ครอปให้ตรงขนาดที่หน่วยงานกำหนด เช่น 1 นิ้ว หรือ 1.5 นิ้ว และให้ศีรษะกับคางอยู่ในกรอบ ③ จัดหลายรูปลงกระดาษ 4×6 นิ้วแผ่นเดียวแล้วไปพิมพ์ที่ร้านหรือตู้พิมพ์รูป ประหยัดกว่าพิมพ์ทีละใบ ส่วนหนังสือเดินทางไทยถ่ายรูปที่สำนักงานตอนยื่นคำร้อง ไม่ต้องเตรียมรูปไปเอง
paras: รูปติดบัตรที่โดนตีกลับส่วนใหญ่ไม่ใช่เพราะกล้องไม่ดี แต่เพราะเงาและสัดส่วน แสงจากเพดานด้านบนทำให้เกิดเงาใต้ตาและคาง แสงจากข้างเดียวทำให้หน้าครึ่งหนึ่งมืด ทางที่ง่ายที่สุดคือหันหน้าเข้าหาหน้าต่างตอนกลางวัน ให้คนอื่นถ่ายในระดับสายตา ไม่ใช้เลนส์มุมกว้างเซลฟี่ใกล้ ๆ เพราะจมูกจะดูใหญ่ผิดสัดส่วน และอย่าใช้ฟิลเตอร์ปรับหน้า

เรื่องขนาด คำว่า 1 นิ้ว หรือ 1.5 นิ้ว ในไทยเป็นชื่อเรียกที่ใช้กันทั่วไป (ราว 2.5×3 ซม. และ 3×4 ซม.) แต่แต่ละหน่วยงานอาจระบุต่างกันเล็กน้อย ส่วนวีซ่าต่างประเทศมักใช้ขนาดเฉพาะ เช่น 35×45 มม. หรือ 2×2 นิ้ว และมักกำหนดสัดส่วนความสูงของศีรษะในรูปด้วย ก่อนครอปให้เปิดประกาศของหน่วยงานที่จะยื่นดูขนาด สีพื้นหลัง และอายุของรูป (เช่น ถ่ายไม่เกิน 6 เดือน) ทุกครั้ง

การพิมพ์คือจุดที่ประหยัดได้มากที่สุด แทนที่จะพิมพ์รูปทีละใบ ให้จัดรูปติดบัตรหลายใบลงกระดาษขนาด 4×6 นิ้วแผ่นเดียว แล้วสั่งพิมพ์เป็นรูปขนาด 4×6 ธรรมดา ได้รูปหลายใบในครั้งเดียว เวลาพิมพ์ต้องเลือกพิมพ์ขนาดจริง ไม่ให้ร้านหรือเครื่องย่อ-ขยายให้พอดีหน้า ไม่อย่างนั้นขนาดจะเพี้ยน
look: ขนาดตรงตามประกาศ: เลือกขนาดสำเร็จรูปหรือกำหนดเองเป็นมม. นิ้ว หรือพิกเซลได้
ตำแหน่งใบหน้า: มีเส้นนำยอดศีรษะ แนวตา และคาง ให้สัดส่วนถูกต้อง
พื้นหลัง: เปลี่ยนเป็นสีขาว ฟ้า หรือสีที่หน่วยงานกำหนดได้โดยไม่ต้องหาผนังใหม่
จัดหน้าพิมพ์: วางหลายรูปลงกระดาษ 4×6 นิ้วหรือ A4 พร้อมเส้นตัด
ความเป็นส่วนตัว: รูปหน้าประมวลผลในเครื่อง ไม่ต้องอัปโหลดขึ้นเว็บที่ไม่รู้จัก
steps: เช็กประกาศของหน่วยงาน: ขนาด สีพื้นหลัง และเงื่อนไขอื่น เช่น ห้ามใส่แว่น
ถ่ายหน้าตรงตอนกลางวัน หันหน้าเข้าหาหน้าต่าง ให้คนอื่นถ่ายในระดับสายตา
ครอปให้ตรงขนาด จัดยอดศีรษะ ตา และคางให้อยู่ในแนวที่กำหนด
เปลี่ยนพื้นหลังเป็นสีตามประกาศ ปรับแสงเล็กน้อยให้เป็นธรรมชาติ
จัดหลายรูปลงกระดาษ 4×6 นิ้วแผ่นเดียว แล้วสั่งพิมพ์แบบขนาดจริงไม่ย่อขยาย
rows: สมัครงานหรือสมัครเรียน
ขนาด 1 นิ้ว หรือ 1.5 นิ้ว ตามที่ระบุ และใบหน้าชัดไม่มีเงา
รูปไม่ตรงขนาดทำให้ต้องพิมพ์ใหม่หรือเอกสารดูไม่เรียบร้อย
ยื่นวีซ่าต่างประเทศ
ขนาดเฉพาะ เช่น 35×45 มม. สัดส่วนศีรษะ และสีพื้นหลัง
สถานทูตหลายแห่งตีกลับรูปที่สัดส่วนหรือพื้นหลังไม่ตรง
ต้องใช้หลายใบ
จัดหลายรูปบนกระดาษ 4×6 นิ้วแผ่นเดียวและพิมพ์ขนาดจริง
ประหยัดกว่าพิมพ์ทีละใบ และได้ขนาดตรงทุกใบ

en.title: Make an ID photo at home: how to shoot, which size, and how to print cheaply
en.meta: Shoot face-on against a plain wall in daylight, crop to the exact size the office asks for, then fit several photos onto one 4×6 inch sheet to print.
en.h1: DIY ID photos: shoot, crop and print to the exact size you need
en.lead: People searching for a free ID photo usually need one quickly for a job, school or paperwork and would rather not visit a studio. You can make one yourself if you know what to check.
en.answer: Three steps: shoot face-on with your phone about half a metre from a plain wall, facing a window so light is even; crop to the exact size required, such as Thailand's common 1-inch or 1.5-inch sizes, with head and chin inside the frame; then place several photos on one 4×6 inch sheet and print it at a photo shop or kiosk, which costs less than printing one by one. Thai passports are photographed at the office when you apply, so you do not bring a photo.
paras: Most rejected ID photos fail on shadows and proportions, not camera quality. Ceiling light casts shadows under the eyes and chin, and light from one side darkens half the face. The easiest fix is to face a window in daytime, have someone else shoot at eye level, avoid close wide-angle selfies that enlarge the nose, and skip beauty filters.

On size, 1 inch and 1.5 inch are common Thai names (about 2.5×3 cm and 3×4 cm), but offices may specify slightly different dimensions. Foreign visas often use specific sizes such as 35×45 mm or 2×2 inches and may also set how tall the head must be. Before cropping, always check the office's notice for size, background colour and how recent the photo must be, for example taken within 6 months.

Printing is where you save most. Instead of printing photos one at a time, put several ID photos on one 4×6 inch layout and print it as a normal 4×6 photo. Make sure it prints at actual size, without the shop or machine scaling it to fit, or the dimensions will drift.

en.fits: Snapport Lite suits people who want to make ID photos themselves on iPhone. It has 35 built-in size templates for 28 countries and regions, or custom sizes in mm, inches or pixels with a chosen DPI. On-device face detection adds guides for top of head, eye line and chin, and the background can switch to white, light grey, blue, red or a custom colour. Export to JPEG, PNG or PDF, or lay out several photos on 4×6 inch, A4 or Letter sheets with cut lines. All templates and editing tools are available and the first export is free. Photos are processed on the device and never uploaded. The app does not guarantee acceptance, so always check the official requirements before submitting.
faq: Do phone ID photos actually work?
For most documents, yes, if the light is even, there are no shadows, the background is plain and the size matches. Some documents, such as Thai passports and ID cards, are photographed at the office.
What is the difference between 1-inch and 1.5-inch photos?
They are common Thai size names: 1 inch is about 2.5×3 cm and 1.5 inch about 3×4 cm. Always use the exact size the office states, since it can vary slightly.
How do I print ID photos cheaply?
Put several photos on one 4×6 inch layout and print it as a normal 4×6 photo at actual size; one print gives you many copies.

loc.title: iPhoneで7zを解凍する方法｜開けない原因と分割・パスワード付きの対処
loc.meta: iPhoneのファイルAppはZIPなら展開できますが、7zは開けません。7z対応アプリで開き、分割ファイル（.7z.001）は全部同じフォルダに置いて先頭から。
loc.h1: 7zを解凍したい：iPhoneで開けないときの原因と手順
loc.lead: メールやダウンロードで届いた「.7z」をタップしても、iPhoneでは中身が見えない。故障でもファイルの破損でもなく、多くの場合は形式の問題です。
loc.answer: iPhone標準のファイルAppが展開できるのは基本的にZIPで、7zには対応していません。7z対応の解凍アプリで開けば中身を確認できます。「.7z.001」「.7z.002」のような分割ファイルは、全部を同じフォルダに保存してから先頭の.001を開きます。パスワード付きの場合は送り主にパスワードを確認し、7zではファイル名自体が暗号化されていることもあるので、入力するまで一覧が見えなくても異常ではありません。
paras: 7zは高い圧縮率で知られる形式で、大きな写真フォルダや資料をまとめて送るときによく使われます。一方で、iPhoneやiPadのファイルAppはZIPの展開には対応していても、7zは対象外です。そのため「タップしてもプレビューが出ない」「共有メニューに開くアプリがない」という状態になります。ファイルが壊れているわけではないので、まずは7zに対応したアプリで開いてみるのが近道です。
開けないときに多いのが分割ファイルです。容量の大きい7zは「〜.7z.001」「〜.7z.002」…と分かれていて、1つでも欠けると最後まで展開できません。メールの添付やクラウドから個別に保存すると、別々の場所に保存されがちです。すべてを同じフォルダにまとめ、ファイル名の番号が連続しているか確認してから、先頭のファイルを開きます。
パスワード付きの7zは、AES-256で暗号化されているのが一般的です。パスワードを忘れた場合、解析して開く方法は現実的ではないので、送り主に確認するしかありません。また、iPhoneの容量にも注意が必要です。展開すると元のファイルより大きくなるため、必要なファイルが1つだけなら全部を展開せず、中身を確認してそのファイルだけ取り出すほうが容量を節約できます。

できません。ファイルAppが展開できるのは基本的にZIPで、7zは対応アプリが必要です。

7zのパスワードを忘れた場合はどうすればいいですか？

en.title: How to extract 7z files on iPhone, including split and password-protected ones
en.meta: The iPhone Files app can unzip ZIP but not 7z. Open it in a 7z-capable app, and for split files (.7z.001) keep every part in one folder and open the first.
en.h1: Extracting 7z on iPhone: why it will not open and what to do
en.lead: You tap a .7z from an email or download and the iPhone shows nothing. The phone is fine and the file is usually fine too; the issue is the format.
en.answer: The built-in Files app on iPhone handles ZIP, not 7z. Open the file in an app that supports 7z and you can see what is inside. For split files named .7z.001, .7z.002 and so on, save every part in the same folder and open .001. For password-protected files, get the password from the sender; 7z can also encrypt file names, so an empty list before you enter it is normal.
paras: 7z is known for strong compression and is often used to send large photo folders or document sets. The Files app on iPhone and iPad extracts ZIP but not 7z, so you get no preview and no app to open it in. The file is not broken; opening it in an app that supports 7z is the quickest fix.

Split archives are a common cause of failure. Large 7z files come as name.7z.001, name.7z.002 and onwards, and if one is missing extraction cannot finish. Saving attachments or cloud files one by one often scatters them across folders. Put them all in one folder, check the numbers run without gaps, then open the first part.

Password-protected 7z files usually use AES-256 encryption. If the password is lost, there is no practical way to crack it, so ask the sender. Also watch storage: extracted files take more space than the archive, so if you only need one file, check the contents and take out just that file instead of extracting everything.

en.fits: Zipbox suits people who need to open 7z and other archives on iPhone. It extracts 13 formats including ZIP, RAR/RAR5, 7z, TAR, GZIP, XZ and ISO, with split and password-protected ZIP, RAR and 7z supported. faq: Can the iPhone Files app extract 7z on its own?
No. The Files app handles ZIP; 7z needs a supporting app.
Can I open just one part of a split 7z?
Extraction needs every part. Save .001 through the last part in one folder, then open the first file.
What if I forgot the 7z password?
Ask the sender. There is no practical way to open an AES-256 encrypted 7z without the password.

loc.title: AIの使用量管理：上限とリセット時刻を先に見て作業を組む方法
loc.meta: Claude・Codex・Copilot・Geminiの使用量管理は「残り％」より「次のリセット時刻」が要。5時間枠と週間上限の考え方、アラートの置き方、複数アカウントの使い分けを整理。
loc.h1: AIの使用量管理：残量より先に「リセット時刻」を見る
loc.lead: 長い作業の途中でAIが上限に達して止まる。原因の多くは使いすぎではなく、どの枠がいつ戻るかを知らないまま重い作業を始めたことにあります。
loc.answer: AIの使用量管理で見るべきものは3つです。①今使っている枠の残り（5時間枠・週間枠・1日の回数など、サービスごとに別）②その枠が次にリセットされる正確な時刻 ③上限に届く手前で知らせる通知。重い作業はリセット直後に始め、残りが少ない枠では軽い作業に回すだけで、途中停止はかなり減らせます。
paras: AIサービスの上限は1種類ではありません。Claudeには5時間のセッション上限と週間上限があり、モデル別の週間上限が加わることもあります。ChatGPTのCodexにも5時間枠と週間枠があり、GitHub Copilotはプレミアムリクエストやチャット、コード補完ごとに、Geminiはモデルごとの1日あたりのリクエスト数で区切られます。「まだ余裕がある」と感じても、止まるのは一番先に尽きる枠です。管理の第一歩は、自分が使うサービスの枠を全部書き出すことです。
次に大事なのはリセット時刻です。残り30％でも10分後に戻るなら気にする必要はなく、残り50％でも週間枠のリセットが4日後なら、大きなリファクタリングや長文の生成は控えたほうが安全です。おすすめは、長い作業を始める前に「どの枠が・何時に戻るか」を確認し、重い作業をリセット直後に寄せる習慣です。通知は90％前後に1本、さらに直前の98％前後にもう1本置くと、作業の区切りをつける時間が取れます。

UsageNowは、Claude・ChatGPT Codex・GitHub Copilot・Geminiの残りと、リセットまでのカウントダウンおよび正確なリセット時刻を表示するアプリです。5時間上限・週間上限・すべての上限を選んで、90や98などのパーセンテージでアラートを作れ、アラートは上限ごと・サイクルごとに1回だけ届きます。リセットアラートで上限が戻った瞬間も分かります。サインインは各サービスの公式ログインページで行い、情報はデバイスのキーチェーンに保存され、アカウント登録やトラッキングはありません。

en.title: Managing AI usage: check limits and reset times before you start
en.meta: Managing Claude, Codex, Copilot and Gemini usage is about the next reset time more than percent left. How 5-hour and weekly limits work, where to set alerts.
en.h1: Managing AI usage: look at the reset time before the percentage
en.lead: An AI stopping halfway through a long task is rarely about using too much. Usually the heavy work started without knowing which limit would run out first, or when it comes back.
en.answer: Managing AI usage comes down to three things: what is left in each limit you use (5-hour window, weekly cap, daily requests, which differ per service), the exact time each one resets, and an alert just before you hit it. Start heavy work right after a reset and keep light tasks for a nearly spent window, and mid-task stops drop sharply.
paras: AI services do not have one limit. Claude has a 5-hour session limit and a weekly limit, sometimes with per-model weekly caps. ChatGPT Codex has a 5-hour window and a weekly window, GitHub Copilot splits premium requests, chat and code completions, and Gemini counts daily requests per model. Whatever feels like plenty, the one that stops you is the limit that runs out first, so the first step is to list every limit you actually depend on.

Then look at reset times. Thirty percent left does not matter if the window resets in ten minutes, while fifty percent left on a weekly cap that resets in four days is a reason to hold off a large refactor or long generation. Check which limit resets when before a long task, and move heavy work to just after a reset. One alert around 90 percent and another around 98 percent gives you time to wrap up cleanly.

UsageNow shows what is left for Claude, ChatGPT Codex, GitHub Copilot and Gemini, with a countdown and the exact reset time. You can build alerts for the 5-hour limit, the weekly limit or all limits at a percentage you choose, such as 90 or 98, and each alert arrives once per limit per cycle. A reset alert tells you the moment a limit is back. Sign-in happens on each service's official login page, credentials stay in the device keychain, and there is no account and no tracking.

faq: Should I watch the 5-hour window or the weekly limit?
Both before a long task. The 5-hour window returns within hours, but a spent weekly limit means waiting days for the reset, so give it more weight later in the week.
What percentage should alerts be set at?
Two levels, around 90 and around 98 percent, leave time to wrap up. In UsageNow you type any percentage per limit and can add as many alerts as you like.
Is it safe to sign in to my AI services?
UsageNow uses each service's official login page and stores sign-in data in the device keychain. There is no UsageNow server; it only talks to the services themselves.

loc.title: Mua sắm bốc đồng: cách dừng lại trước khi bấm chốt đơn
loc.meta: Mua sắm bốc đồng hay đến từ sale chớp nhoáng, livestream và giỏ hàng đầy sẵn. Quy giá ra giờ làm việc, gắn nhãn Cần, Muốn, Bốc đồng và chờ trước khi thanh toán.
loc.h1: Mua sắm bốc đồng: ba bước dừng lại trước khi chốt đơn
loc.lead: Phần lớn món đồ mua bốc đồng không đắt. Chúng nhỏ, đến nhanh và cộng dồn lại mỗi tháng, đến lúc nhìn sao kê mới thấy hối hận.
loc.answer: Muốn bớt mua sắm bốc đồng, hãy chèn một khoảng dừng giữa lúc muốn và lúc trả tiền: quy giá ra số giờ làm việc theo lương thực nhận, tự hỏi món này là Cần, Muốn hay Bốc đồng, và với món không cần gấp thì để trong giỏ ít nhất 24 giờ. Sau vài tuần ghi lại, bạn sẽ thấy rõ danh mục nào đang ngốn nhiều giờ làm việc nhất.
paras: Mua bốc đồng hiếm khi là do thiếu kỷ luật. Nó đến từ những tình huống được thiết kế để bạn quyết nhanh: đồng hồ đếm ngược của sale chớp nhoáng, ngày sale lớn như 11.11 hay 12.12, livestream có người chốt đơn liên tục, mã giảm giá sắp hết hạn, hay thẻ đã lưu sẵn chỉ cần một chạm. Trong vài giây đó, bạn so giá với giá gốc chứ không so với số tiền mình phải làm ra, nên mọi món đều trông như hời.

Cách hiệu quả là đổi đơn vị so sánh. Lấy lương thực nhận một tháng chia cho số giờ làm thực tế để ra lương theo giờ, rồi quy giá món đồ ra giờ. Một chiếc áo 450.000 đồng nghe nhẹ nhàng, nhưng nếu bạn kiếm 50.000 đồng một giờ thì đó là chín giờ làm việc, hơn một ngày công. Sau đó gắn nhãn thật lòng: Cần (thiếu thì ảnh hưởng sinh hoạt), Muốn (thích nhưng chờ được) hay Bốc đồng (vừa thấy là muốn). Món Muốn để 24 giờ, món Bốc đồng để ít nhất ba ngày rồi mới quyết.

HoursTag Lite làm đúng phần quy đổi và ghi nhận này. Bạn nhập lương thực nhận theo giờ, ứng dụng quy mọi mức giá ra thời gian làm việc, cho gắn nhãn Cần, Muốn hay Bốc đồng cho từng lần mua và cho xem mỗi danh mục đã ngốn bao nhiêu giờ làm việc. Nếu đang tiết kiệm cho một mục tiêu, bạn xem được cần làm bao nhiêu giờ cho nó và theo dõi tiến độ. Mọi dữ liệu nằm trên thiết bị, không cần tài khoản, không theo dõi.

faq: Làm sao biết mình đang mua sắm bốc đồng?

Dấu hiệu thường gặp: mua vì đồng hồ đếm ngược hay mã sắp hết hạn, không định mua trước khi mở ứng dụng, và vài ngày sau ít dùng đến. Gắn nhãn mỗi lần mua trong vài tuần sẽ cho bạn câu trả lời rõ hơn cảm giác.
Quy giá ra giờ làm việc thì dùng lương nào?
Dùng lương thực nhận, tức số tiền về tài khoản sau thuế và bảo hiểm, chia cho số giờ làm thực tế. Dùng lương gộp sẽ làm mọi món trông rẻ hơn thực tế.
Quy tắc chờ 24 giờ có thật sự hiệu quả?
Nó tách lúc hứng khởi khỏi lúc trả tiền. Nhiều món sau một ngày không còn hấp dẫn; món vẫn muốn sau khi chờ thường là món bạn sẽ dùng thật.

en.title: Impulse shopping: how to pause before you hit checkout
en.meta: Impulse buys come from flash sales, livestreams and a full cart. Convert the price into work hours, label it need, want or impulse, and wait before you pay.
en.h1: Impulse shopping: three steps to pause before checkout
en.lead: Most impulse buys are not expensive. They are small, fast and add up every month, and the regret shows up only when you read the statement.
en.answer: To cut impulse shopping, put a pause between wanting and paying: convert the price into hours of work at your take-home rate, ask whether it is a need, a want or an impulse, and leave anything non-urgent in the cart for at least 24 hours. After a few weeks of labels you will see which category eats the most work hours.
paras: Impulse buying is rarely a lack of discipline. It comes from moments built for quick decisions: flash-sale countdowns, big sale days such as 11.11 and 12.12, livestreams where someone keeps closing orders, a voucher about to expire, a saved card that needs one tap. In those seconds you compare the price with the original price, not with the money you have to earn, so everything looks like a bargain.

The fix is to change the unit. Divide monthly take-home pay by the hours you actually work to get an hourly rate, then convert the price into hours. A 450,000-dong shirt sounds light, but at 50,000 dong an hour it is nine hours of work, more than a full day. Then label it honestly: need (life is harder without it), want (nice, but can wait) or impulse (wanted it the moment you saw it). Give wants 24 hours and impulses at least three days.

HoursTag Lite handles this conversion and labeling. You enter your take-home hourly pay, it converts any price into work time, lets you tag each purchase as need, want or impulse, and shows how many work hours each category has used. If you are saving for something, you see the hours behind the goal and track progress. Everything stays on the device, with no account and no tracking.

It has a Home Screen widget and Apple Watch support, plus backup and restore for income, spending, goals and settings. The first three conversions need no purchase; an optional one-time in-app purchase unlocks unlimited conversions and logging.
faq: How do I know I am impulse shopping?

Common signs: buying because of a countdown or expiring voucher, not planning to buy before opening the app, and barely using it days later. Labeling every purchase for a few weeks gives a clearer answer than a feeling.
Which pay should I use to convert prices into hours?
Take-home pay, the amount that lands after tax and insurance, divided by hours actually worked. Gross pay makes everything look cheaper than it really is.
Does the 24-hour rule really work?
It separates the moment of excitement from the moment of paying. Many items lose their pull after a day; what you still want after waiting is usually something you will use.

loc.title: 儿童习惯怎么养成：3–7 岁一次只练一个日常任务
loc.meta: 3–7 岁儿童好习惯怎么养：一次只练一个日常任务，拆成两三个小步骤，做完马上具体表扬，固定时间每天重复。附吃饭、刷牙、收玩具、睡前的练习顺序。
loc.h1: 3–7 岁儿童习惯养成：一次一个任务，做完马上鼓励
loc.lead: 孩子不肯刷牙、吃饭磨蹭、玩具不收，很多家长的第一反应是多讲几遍。可是对三到七岁的孩子来说，唠叨越多，越像是大人的事，不是自己的事。
loc.answer: 3–7 岁儿童养成习惯，关键是“少、短、快”：一次只练一个日常任务，把它拆成两三个看得见的小步骤，孩子每完成一步就马上给具体的鼓励，并且每天在同一个时间做。等这个任务连续几周不用提醒也能完成，再加下一个。
paras: 这个年龄的孩子还很难为“以后会怎样”而坚持，他们在意的是当下有没有回应。所以周末才兑现的奖励，对三四岁的孩子往往太远。更有效的是在动作刚完成时，就说出具体的事：“你自己把牙刷放回杯子里了”，比一句“真棒”更能让孩子知道下次该做什么。奖励可以小，但要及时、要和行为对得上。
习惯是练出来的顺序，而不是一次讲清楚的道理。建议从最容易成功的任务开始，例如收玩具或睡前刷牙，固定在每天同一个时间点，把步骤拆成“挤牙膏、刷两分钟、漱口”这样的小块。前一两周家长陪着做，之后慢慢只提醒第一步。同时开始三四个新习惯，孩子和大人都容易放弃；一个稳定了再加一个，进度反而更快。
Lumi 任务星球就是围绕这种即时反馈设计的亲子工具。吃饭、刷牙、睡觉、收玩具、上学准备都是每日任务，孩子每完成一小步点一下屏幕，兔兔伙伴会立刻欢呼，整个任务完成时全星球一起庆祝。伙伴会用孩子的小名打招呼并一天天长大，还有一百个成就贴纸可以收集。家长后台能看今日总览、七天日历和完整完成记录。

faq: 一个儿童习惯大概要多久才能养成？
因孩子和任务而异，通常需要几周的每天重复。比天数更重要的是固定时间和及时鼓励；看到孩子不用提醒也会主动开始，就可以加下一个任务了。
用奖励会不会让孩子只为了奖励才做？
关键在于奖励是否及时、是否和具体行为挂钩，并且搭配具体的表扬。随着动作变成习惯，可以慢慢减少提醒，让完成本身成为孩子的成就感。
几岁开始用习惯任务比较合适？
三岁左右孩子已能理解“做完一步就点一下”的规则。Lumi 任务星球是给家长的工具，设计成亲子一起使用，适合三到七岁的孩子。

en.title: Building habits in kids aged 3 to 7: one routine at a time
en.meta: How to build good habits in children aged three to seven: one routine at a time, split into two or three steps, specific praise right away, same time every day.
en.h1: Habits for kids aged 3 to 7: one task at a time, praise right after
en.lead: When a child won't brush, dawdles over dinner or leaves toys out, most parents explain it again. For a three- to seven-year-old, more talking makes it the adult's job, not theirs.
en.answer: Habits at three to seven come from keeping it small, short and immediate: practise one daily task at a time, split it into two or three visible steps, give specific encouragement the moment each step is done, and do it at the same time every day. Add the next task only once this one happens for a few weeks without reminders.
paras: Children this age struggle to persist for something later; what matters is a response now. A reward that arrives at the weekend is often too far away for a three- or four-year-old. It works better to name the action right as it is finished: "You put your toothbrush back in the cup yourself" tells a child what to repeat far better than "good job". Rewards can be small, but they should be quick and tied to the behaviour.

A habit is a practised sequence, not an explanation given once. Start with the task most likely to succeed, such as tidying toys or brushing before bed, fix it to the same moment each day, and break it into pieces like "toothpaste, brush for two minutes, rinse". Do it together for the first week or two, then only prompt the first step. Starting three or four new habits at once tends to make both child and parent give up; stabilise one, then add the next.

Lumi Mission Planet is a parent tool built around this kind of instant feedback. Eating, brushing, bedtime, tidying toys and getting ready for school are daily missions; each time the child finishes a small step they tap the screen and the bunny companion cheers at once, and the whole planet celebrates when the mission is done. Companions greet the child by nickname and grow day by day, and there are a hundred achievement stickers to collect. The parent dashboard shows today's overview, a seven-day calendar and the full completion history.

faq: How long does it take a child to form a habit?
It varies by child and task, usually a few weeks of daily repetition. Fixed timing and prompt encouragement matter more than a day count; when your child starts without a reminder, add the next task.
Will rewards make my child do it only for the reward?
What matters is that rewards are prompt, tied to a specific action and paired with specific praise. As the action becomes routine you can reduce prompts so finishing becomes the achievement itself.

Around three, children can follow the rule "finish a step, tap once". Lumi Mission Planet is a tool for parents, designed to be used together with children aged three to seven.

loc.title: 一頁摘要怎麼寫：結論先講、三個重點、一個下一步
loc.meta: 一頁摘要不是把資料縮小，而是先寫結論，再用三個重點和數字撐住，最後寫要對方做的決定。附會議紀錄、報告、課程重點濃縮成一頁的步驟。
loc.h1: 一頁摘要的寫法：結論在最上面，讀的人 30 秒看完
loc.lead: 多數一頁摘要寫不好，不是字太多，而是照時間順序把資料縮小。讀的人看到最後才知道你要說什麼，而主管通常不會看到最後。
loc.answer: 一頁摘要用「結論 → 三個重點 → 下一步」的順序寫：標題直接寫成一句結論，下面放三個支撐重點，每個重點盡量配一個數字或事實，最後一行寫需要對方決定或配合的事。寫不進這個框架的內容，放附件，不硬塞進這一頁。
paras: 先寫結論，是因為讀一頁摘要的人通常只有幾十秒。「第三季營收報告」是主題，不是結論；「第三季營收成長 12%，主要來自新客，但回購率下滑需要處理」才是結論。標題寫成一句完整的話，讀者只看標題也知道重點，後面的內容只是在證明這句話。
重點以三個為上限。超過三個，讀者記不住，你也會開始放「順便一提」的資訊。每個重點要能回答「所以呢」：數字放在句子裡，而不是只貼一張表；有趨勢就用折線，有比較就用對照，有步驟就用流程。最後一定要有下一步，例如「請在週五前決定是否加碼預算」，否則一頁摘要只是一份讀完就忘的報告。
OnePage PPT 適合把手上的素材直接整理成這樣的一頁。打字、貼上段落、螢幕截圖、照片、PDF 或 CSV 表格都可以放進去，點「產生投影片」，內容會被整理成標題重點，排成一頁 16:9 投影片；數字會變成直條圖、折線圖等圖表，步驟變成流程圖，日期變成時間軸，而且只有在資料撐得住時才畫圖，不會自行編造數字。

faq: 一頁摘要和懶人包有什麼不同？
懶人包通常把資訊整理得好讀，一頁摘要則多了立場：先下結論，再用重點證明，最後要對方做決定。寫的時候問自己「讀完之後我希望對方做什麼」。
資料太多塞不進一頁怎麼辦？
不要縮字或縮圖。先確定結論，只留下能直接支撐它的三個重點，其他細節放附件或備註，需要時再拿出來。
一頁摘要一定要有圖表嗎？
不一定。只有在數字真的能說明趨勢或差異時才放圖表；資料撐不住時，三句清楚的重點比一張勉強的圖更好讀。

en.title: How to write a one-page summary: conclusion first, three points
en.meta: A one-page summary is not shrunken material: lead with the conclusion, back it with three points and numbers, end with the decision you need from the reader.
en.h1: Writing a one-page summary: conclusion on top, read in 30 seconds
en.lead: Most one-page summaries fail not because of length but because they shrink the material in chronological order. The reader finds the point only at the end, and a busy manager rarely gets there.
en.answer: Write a one-page summary as conclusion, three points, next step: make the title a one-sentence conclusion, add three supporting points each with a number or fact where possible, and close with the one decision or action you need from the reader. Anything that does not fit that frame goes in an appendix, not onto the page.
paras: The conclusion goes first because a one-page reader often has only a few seconds. "Q3 revenue report" is a topic, not a conclusion; "Q3 revenue grew 12 percent, mostly from new customers, but repeat purchases fell and need attention" is a conclusion. Make the title a full sentence so a reader who only sees the title still gets the point, and let the rest of the page prove it.

Cap the supporting points at three. Beyond that readers stop remembering and you start adding by-the-way details. Each point should answer "so what": put the number inside the sentence instead of pasting a table, use a line for trends, a side-by-side for comparisons and a flow for steps. Always end with a next step, such as "please decide by Friday whether to raise the budget", or the page becomes a report people forget.

OnePage PPT is built to turn raw material into that kind of single page. Typed text, pasted paragraphs, screenshots, photos, PDFs and CSV tables can all go in; tap Generate Slide and the content is organized into headline points on one 16:9 slide. Numbers become bar or line charts, steps become flowcharts and dates become timelines, and a chart is drawn only when the data supports it, never with invented numbers.

Whether supporting points are kept to three or fewer
Whether each point carries a number or fact instead of adjectives
Whether each chart type matches the data: trend, comparison, steps, dates
Whether the final line states the decision or next step you need
steps: Write the conclusion as one sentence and use it as the title
Pick the three points from your material that best prove it
Give each point a number, date or concrete fact
Choose the visual by data type: line for trends, side-by-side for comparisons, flow for steps
End with the decision or action you need, and move the rest to an appendix

en.fits: OnePage PPT suits consultants, students, teachers and project managers who need to turn meeting notes, quarterly data, interview notes or lesson points into one page. There are no templates to pick; six one-tap restyles such as cleaner, more visual and more professional rearrange the page, and elements you like can be locked. Tap any element to rewrite text or swap an image, with full version history. Export editable .pptx, PDF and high-resolution PNG; processing happens on the device and works offline.
faq: How is a one-page summary different from a digest?
A digest makes information easy to read; a one-page summary takes a position: conclusion first, points as proof, a decision at the end. Ask yourself what you want the reader to do after reading.
What if the material will not fit on one page?
Do not shrink fonts or charts. Fix the conclusion, keep only the three points that directly support it, and move the remaining detail to an appendix or notes.
Does a one-page summary need a chart?
No. Use a chart only when numbers really show a trend or difference; when the data cannot carry one, three clear sentences read better than a forced graphic.

loc.h1: Horloge flip sur iPhone ou iPad : les réglages qui comptent vraiment
loc.lead: Une horloge flip plein écran sur un téléphone en charge, c’est joli le premier soir. Le deuxième, l’écran s’éteint tout seul, éclaire trop la chambre ou laisse craindre un marquage de la dalle.
loc.answer: Pour utiliser un iPhone ou un iPad comme horloge flip, réglez trois choses : l’écran doit rester allumé (au moins pendant la charge, sinon le verrouillage automatique l’éteint), la nuit il faut un cadran sombre, idéalement rouge tamisé sur fond noir, et sur un écran OLED il faut éviter une image totalement fixe pendant des heures, avec un léger déplacement des pixels.
paras: L’horloge flip reprend l’affichage à palettes des vieux réveils et des panneaux de gare : de grands chiffres lisibles de loin, qui basculent à chaque minute. Sur iPhone, le mode StandBy affiche déjà une horloge quand le téléphone est en charge, posé à l’horizontale et verrouillé, mais selon le modèle l’écran peut s’éteindre au bout d’un moment. Pour un affichage permanent au bureau ou sur une étagère, il faut une app capable de garder l’écran allumé sans que vous désactiviez le verrouillage automatique pour tout le téléphone.

Dans la chambre, la luminosité compte plus que le style. Un cadran blanc sur fond clair éclaire la pièce ; un cadran rouge tamisé sur fond noir pur reste lisible et gêne beaucoup moins. Sur les écrans OLED, le noir pur éteint réellement les pixels, mais un chiffre immobile affiché toute la nuit, chaque nuit, augmente le risque de rémanence : un déplacement discret des pixels et des détails adoucis limitent ce risque. Pensez aussi à la batterie : un seuil au-dessus duquel l’écran reste allumé évite de vider un téléphone mal branché.

Stay Clock transforme un iPhone ou un iPad en horloge toujours allumée, lisible depuis l’autre bout de la pièce, avec 101 cadrans dont des horloges flip. L’écran peut rester allumé pendant la charge, au-dessus d’un seuil de batterie, ou suivre le réglage système. La nuit, un cadran rouge sombre sur fond noir pur et un déplacement discret des pixels protègent les dalles OLED. Le même cadran apparaît sur StandBy, l’écran verrouillé, les widgets de l’écran d’accueil et l’Apple Watch.

en.title: Flip clock on iPhone or iPad: desk, bedside and OLED screens
en.meta: Turn an iPhone or old iPad into a flip clock: screen on while charging, a dim red face at night and a protected OLED panel. The settings that matter.
en.h1: Flip clock on iPhone or iPad: the settings that actually matter
en.lead: A full-screen flip clock on a charging phone looks great the first night. By the second, the screen has switched itself off, lights up the bedroom, or you start worrying about burn-in.
en.answer: To use an iPhone or iPad as a flip clock, get three things right: the screen has to stay on (at least while charging, or Auto-Lock turns it off), at night you need a dark face, ideally dim red on pure black, and on an OLED screen you should avoid a completely static image for hours, using a slight pixel shift.
paras: A flip clock borrows the split-flap look of old alarm clocks and station boards: big digits readable from across the room that flip over each minute. On iPhone, StandBy already shows a clock when the phone is charging, on its side and locked, but depending on the model the screen may turn off after a while. For a permanent display on a desk or shelf you need an app that keeps the screen on without switching off Auto-Lock for the whole phone.

In the bedroom, brightness matters more than style. A white face on a light background lights the room; a dim red face on pure black stays readable and disturbs far less. On OLED screens pure black really turns pixels off, but a motionless digit shown all night, every night, raises the risk of burn-in; a subtle pixel shift and softened details reduce it. Think about the battery too: a threshold above which the screen stays on avoids draining a phone that is not properly plugged in.

Stay Clock turns an iPhone or iPad into an always-on clock readable from across the room, with 101 faces including flip clocks. The screen can stay on while charging, above a battery threshold, or follow the system setting. At night a dim red face on pure black and a subtle pixel shift protect OLED panels. The same face appears in StandBy, on the Lock Screen, in Home Screen widgets and on Apple Watch.

StandBy shows a clock while the iPhone is charging, on its side and locked, but depending on the model the screen may turn off after a while. For a permanent display or an iPad, a clock app that keeps the screen on is more reliable.
Does leaving the clock on all night damage an OLED screen?
A strictly static image for hours, night after night, raises the risk of burn-in. A pure black background, low brightness and a slight pixel shift reduce that risk a lot.
Can an old iPad be used as a flip clock?
Yes, it is a good use: plugged in on a shelf it shows the time in large digits. Stay Clock is built for iPhone and iPad.

loc.title: Filter phim trên iPhone: chọn tông film theo ánh sáng, không theo trend
loc.meta: Filter phim đẹp hay không phụ thuộc vào ánh sáng lúc chụp. Cách chọn tông film cho nắng gắt, trời âm u và phố đêm, dùng hạt film, quầng sáng, rò sáng vừa đủ mà da vẫn tự nhiên.
loc.h1: Filter phim trên iPhone: chọn theo ánh sáng, đừng chọn theo trend
loc.lead: Cùng một filter phim, ảnh chụp lúc 4 giờ chiều trông rất có hồn, còn ảnh chụp giữa trưa lại bệt màu và da xám. Vấn đề thường không nằm ở filter mà ở việc chọn sai tông cho ánh sáng.
loc.answer: Muốn dùng filter phim cho đẹp, hãy chọn tông theo ánh sáng: nắng gắt hợp tông ấm, tương phản nhẹ; trời âm u hợp tông có màu đậm hơn; phố đêm hợp quầng sáng quanh đèn. Sau đó chỉ thêm một hai hiệu ứng như hạt film hoặc rò sáng, và kiểm tra lại màu da trước khi lưu.
paras: Người tìm “filter phim” thường muốn ảnh trông như chụp bằng máy film: màu dịu, có hạt, có chút hoài niệm. Nhưng film thật cũng phản ứng khác nhau với từng kiểu ánh sáng. Nắng trưa ở Việt Nam rất gắt, nếu chồng thêm tương phản mạnh thì vùng sáng cháy và bóng đen đặc lại. Trời mưa, âm u thì ngược lại, ảnh dễ bị nhạt, cần tông có màu đậm hơn một chút.

Cách dễ nhất là xem trước. PhotoCream có hơn 100 tông film với hạt film, quầng sáng, rò sáng và viền tối, xem trực tiếp ngay trước khi bấm chụp, nên bạn có thể đổi tông theo ánh sáng tại chỗ thay vì chụp xong mới thử. Nếu đã có một bức ảnh mình thích, tính năng trộm phong cách sẽ phân tích màu ngay trên máy và biến chúng thành tông màu film có thể chỉnh sửa để áp dụng cho ảnh của bạn.

Chụp người thì đừng để filter làm hỏng da. Sau khi chọn tông, tinh chỉnh bằng đường cong, HSL và tách tông; dùng làm mịn da mà mắt và tóc vẫn sắc nét. Muốn ảnh giống film xưa hơn, thêm dấu ngày, khung, hạt hoặc bụi, nhưng chọn một hai thứ thôi. Mọi thứ đều xử lý trên máy, ảnh không bị tải lên.

faq: Vì sao cùng một filter phim mà ảnh lúc đẹp lúc xấu?
Vì ánh sáng khác nhau. Nắng gắt, trời âm u và ánh đèn đêm cần tông film khác nhau; chọn tông theo ánh sáng sẽ ổn định hơn nhiều.
Thêm nhiều hiệu ứng có làm ảnh giống film hơn không?
Thường là không. Hạt film, rò sáng, quầng sáng, bụi nên dùng một hai thứ mỗi ảnh; chồng hết lên nhau ảnh sẽ rối.
Làm sao để da không bị xám khi dùng filter phim?
Chỉnh lại sắc da bằng HSL hoặc đường cong sau khi chọn tông, và làm mịn da vừa phải để mắt, tóc vẫn sắc nét.

en.title: Film filter on iPhone: pick the film look for the light, not the trend
en.meta: Whether a film filter looks good depends on the light. How to pick a film look for harsh sun, overcast days and night streets, with just enough grain, halation and light leaks while skin stays natural.
en.h1: Film filter on iPhone: choose for the light, not for the trend
en.lead: The same film filter makes a 4 p.m. shot look full of character and a midday shot look flat with grey skin. The filter is usually not the problem; the look just does not suit the light.
en.answer: To make a film filter work, choose the look for the light: harsh sun suits a warm look with soft contrast, overcast days suit a slightly richer look, and night streets suit halation around the lights. Then add only one or two effects such as grain or a light leak, and check skin tones before saving.
paras: People searching for a film filter usually want photos that look shot on film: soft colors, grain, a bit of nostalgia. But real film also reacts differently to each kind of light. Midday sun in the tropics is harsh, and stacking strong contrast on top blows out highlights and crushes shadows. Rainy, overcast days are the opposite: photos turn pale and need a slightly richer look.

The easiest fix is previewing. PhotoCream has 100+ film looks with grain, halation, light leaks and vignette, previewed live before you shoot, so you can switch looks to match the light on the spot instead of experimenting afterwards. If you already have a photo you love, Steal the Look reads its colors on your device and turns them into an editable film grade you can apply to your own shots.

For portraits, do not let the filter ruin skin. After picking a look, fine-tune with curves, HSL and split toning, and smooth skin while eyes and hair stay sharp. For a more old-film feel, add a date stamp, border, grain or dust, but pick one or two. Everything is processed on your device and nothing is uploaded.

Text, borders, grain, dust and a date stamp add the old-film touch. Everything is processed on your device, nothing is uploaded and no account is needed.
faq: Why does the same film filter look great one time and bad the next?
Because the light changes. Harsh sun, overcast days and night lights each need a different film look; choosing for the light makes results far more consistent.
Do more effects make a photo look more like film?
Usually not. Use one or two of grain, light leaks, halation or dust per photo; stacking all of them makes it messy.
How do I keep skin from turning grey with a film filter?
Correct skin tones with HSL or curves after choosing the look, and use light skin smoothing so eyes and hair stay sharp.

loc.answer: บันทึกงานบ้านควรจดเฉพาะงานที่ทำห่างกันเป็นสัปดาห์หรือเป็นเดือน และลืมง่าย เช่น ล้างแผ่นกรองแอร์ เปลี่ยนไส้กรองน้ำ ซักผ้าปูที่นอนและผ้าม่าน ทำเสร็จแล้วบันทึกวันที่ทันที และตั้งรอบให้วันถัดไปนับจากวันที่ทำจริง ไม่ใช่จากวันที่วางแผนไว้
paras: คนที่ค้นหา “บันทึกงานบ้าน” มักเคยลองจดในสมุดหรือโน้ตแล้วเลิกไปภายในสองสัปดาห์ เพราะจดทุกอย่างจนเหนื่อย งานประจำวันไม่จำเป็นต้องจด สิ่งที่คุ้มค่าคืองานที่ทำห่างกันนาน ในบ้านเมืองร้อนอย่างไทย แอร์ทำงานแทบทั้งปี แผ่นกรองแอร์จึงตันเร็วกว่าที่คิด ช่วงหน้าฝนผ้าม่านและผ้าปูที่นอนอับชื้นง่าย ส่วนไส้กรองน้ำก็มีอายุการใช้งานของมัน

en.title: Household chore log: which chores to record and how often in a hot climate
en.meta: A chore log works when you skip the daily tasks and record the easy-to-forget ones, like cleaning the AC filter, changing the water filter or washing curtains, with the next date counted from when you actually did it.
en.h1: Household chore log: record only what you forget, and count from the day you did it
en.lead: Nobody forgets the dishes. What gets forgotten are the jobs done a few times a year, until the AC starts to smell or the filtered water tastes off and you cannot remember when you last dealt with it.
en.answer: A household chore log should only hold chores done weeks or months apart that are easy to forget, such as cleaning the AC filter, changing the water filter and washing sheets and curtains. Log the date the moment you finish, and set a rhythm so the next date counts from the day you actually did it, not the day you planned.
paras: People looking for a chore log have often tried a notebook or notes app and quit within two weeks because they were recording everything. Daily chores do not need logging. The ones worth it are the long-gap jobs. In a hot climate the AC runs almost all year, so its filter clogs faster than you expect; in the rainy season curtains and sheets get damp quickly; and water filters have a working life of their own.

The key is logging when you finish, not reconstructing it later. In Mochi DoneStamp, tap once when a chore is done and it records the exact time, so you always see how long it has been. If you forgot to tap on the day, you can backdate, edit or delete any occurrence, and a wrong tap can be undone right away.

After a while, set a rhythm for the repeating ones. Rhythms can be flexible or exact, from minutes to years, and the next date always counts from the day you actually did it. When it is due, a local reminder arrives with Done and Snooze actions. Add an optional note or photo, such as the filter model, and use interval insights to see how many days apart you really do it.
look: Can you log a chore in one tap when you finish?
Can you add or edit a past date for the day you forgot?
Does the next date count from when you did it or from the plan?

Does the data stay on the device with no account needed?
steps: Pick 3–5 chores that are done far apart and easy to forget.
Next time you finish one, tap to log it right away.
If you remember roughly when you last did it, backdate that as a starting point.
Set a rhythm for each chore and turn on reminders.
Put a widget on the Home Screen to see which chores are coming due.
rows: A short rhythm while the AC runs daily
A clogged filter cools slowly and smells
Last change date and the model used
Filters wear out; left too long, water can taste off
A shorter rhythm in the rainy season
en.fits: Mochi DoneStamp suits anyone who wants to know when each chore was last done without keeping a notebook. One-tap logging, interactive Home and Lock Screen widgets, Siri and Shortcuts, and Apple Watch to see the last time and log it from your wrist. Complete backup and JSON export are included. No account, no ads, no analytics, no tracking; your core data stays on your device.
faq: Should I log every chore?
No. You remember the daily ones anyway. Logging only chores done weeks or months apart keeps the habit going much longer.
Why should the next date count from when I actually did it?
If you did it three days late, the next one should shift too; otherwise reminders come too early and get ignored.
I forgot to log it on the day. Can I fix that later?
Yes. In Mochi DoneStamp you can backdate, edit or delete any occurrence at any time.

loc.title: 旅程表の作り方：当日に本当に役立つのは「時刻・移動・空き時間」
loc.meta: 旅程表はきれいに作るより、当日に見て迷わないことが大事。時刻、移動手段、予定と予定のあいだの空き時間、予約情報を日ごとにまとめる作り方と、表計算で作るときの落とし穴。
loc.h1: 旅程表の作り方：当日に迷わないための列はこれだけ
loc.lead: 表計算アプリで作った旅程表は、出発前夜には完璧に見えます。ところが旅先で電車が遅れると、どの予定をずらせばいいのか、スマホの小さな画面では読み取れません。
loc.answer: 旅程表は、日ごとに「時刻・予定・移動・空き時間・予約情報」の5つがそろっていれば十分です。特に予定と予定のあいだの空き時間を見えるようにしておくと、遅れが出たときにどこで調整できるかがすぐ分かります。
paras: 「旅程表」で検索する人の多くは、テンプレートを探しています。ただ、列を増やすほど当日は読みにくくなります。旅先で見るのは「次は何時にどこへ行くか」と「それに間に合うか」の2点です。時刻と予定のほかに、移動時間と、予定のあいだにどれだけ余裕があるかが分かれば、乗り遅れや遅延にも落ち着いて対応できます。
表計算での旅程表は、空き時間を自分で計算する必要があり、予定を1つずらすと後ろの時刻を全部直すことになります。TripBee Lite では、朝のフライト、移動、観光、ホテルのチェックイン、夕食までを1日1本のタイムラインに時間順に並べると、予定と予定のあいだの空き時間が自動で計算されます。
予約番号やチケットの情報は、別のメールやスクリーンショットに散らばりがちです。TripBee Lite ではフライトやホテル、チケットの情報とメモをその日の予定にまとめて保存でき、出発前にはカウントダウンと旅先の天気も確認できます。旅行中は次の予定を Apple Watch ですぐに確認でき、スマホを取り出さずに済みます。

予定と予定のあいだの空き時間が見えるか
移動手段と移動時間が予定と一緒に書かれているか
予約番号やチケット情報がその日の予定と一緒にあるか

空き時間が短すぎる所は予定を1つ減らす

loc.fits: TripBee Lite は、旅程表を表計算ではなくスマホで作りたい人に向いています。毎日を1本のタイムラインにまとめ、空き時間は自動計算。フライトやホテル、チケットの情報とメモはその日の予定に保存でき、カウントダウンと旅先の天気、Apple Watch での次の予定の確認にも対応しています。アカウント登録は不要で、広告、解析、トラッキングはありません。
faq: 旅程表に最低限必要な項目は？
日付、時刻、予定、移動手段、予約情報の5つです。さらに予定のあいだの空き時間が分かると、当日の調整がずっと楽になります。
表計算アプリで旅程表を作るのはだめですか？
作れますが、予定を1つずらすと後ろの時刻を全部直す必要があり、スマホでは読みにくくなりがちです。旅行中に見るなら、時間順のタイムライン形式のほうが扱いやすいです。
空き時間はどれくらいあればいいですか？
乗り換えや移動のある予定のあとには余裕を多めに取るのが安心です。空き時間が見えていれば、短すぎる所で予定を1つ減らす判断がしやすくなります。

en.title: How to make a travel itinerary: the columns that actually help on the day
en.meta: A good itinerary is less about looking neat and more about not getting lost on the day. Organize times, transport, the gaps between plans and booking details by day, and avoid the spreadsheet traps.
en.h1: How to make a travel itinerary: the only columns you need on the day
en.lead: A spreadsheet itinerary looks perfect the night before you leave. Then a train runs late and, on a small phone screen, you cannot tell which plan to move.
en.answer: An itinerary needs five things per day: time, plan, transport, the gap until the next stop, and booking details. Making the gaps between plans visible is what lets you see where to adjust when something runs late.
paras: Most people searching for an itinerary template want columns, but every extra column makes it harder to read on the day. On the road you only check two things: where you are going next and when, and whether you will make it. With times and plans plus travel time and the slack between stops, you can handle a missed connection or a delay calmly.

In a spreadsheet you calculate the gaps yourself, and moving one plan means fixing every time after it. In TripBee Lite you put each day on one timeline, from the morning flight, transfers and sights to hotel check-in and dinner, in order, and the gaps between stops are worked out for you.

Booking numbers and ticket details tend to be scattered across emails and screenshots. TripBee Lite keeps flight, hotel and ticket details and notes with the day they belong to, and shows a countdown and local weather before you go. During the trip you can see your next stop right on Apple Watch without pulling out your phone.
look: Is each day in time order so the next plan is obvious?
Can you see the gaps between plans?
Are transport and travel time written next to each plan?
Are booking numbers and ticket details kept with that day?
Is it readable on a small phone or watch screen?
steps: Make one block per day of the trip.
Add the fixed plans first: flights, check-ins, booked meals.
Fill sights and shopping in between, in time order.
Where a gap is too short, drop one plan.
Attach booking numbers and ticket details as notes on that day.
rows: You see what is next at a glance
Shows where you can adjust when running late
Flight, hotel and ticket numbers and notes
No searching at the counter or check-in
en.fits: TripBee Lite suits people who would rather build an itinerary on their phone than in a spreadsheet. Each day sits on one timeline with the gaps worked out automatically. Flight, hotel and ticket details and notes stay with their day, with a countdown, local weather and your next stop on Apple Watch. No account is required, and there are no ads, analytics or tracking.
faq: What does an itinerary need at minimum?
Date, time, plan, transport and booking details. Seeing the gaps between plans as well makes adjusting on the day much easier.
Is a spreadsheet itinerary a bad idea?
It works, but moving one plan means fixing every time after it, and it is hard to read on a phone. For use during the trip, a time-ordered timeline is easier.
How much gap should I leave?
Leave more slack after plans that involve transfers or travel. When the gaps are visible, it is easy to spot where one plan should go.

loc.title: Zhuyin lernen: Ihr Kind kennt die Zeichen, kann aber keine Silbe lesen – was hilft
loc.meta: Viele Kinder erkennen einzelne Bopomofo-Zeichen, bleiben aber beim Zusammenschleifen hängen. Wie Sie Anlaut, Mittellaut und Auslaut zu Hause zu Silben verbinden und den Ton erst danach setzen.
loc.h1: Zhuyin lernen: vom einzelnen Zeichen zur gelesenen Silbe
loc.lead: Ihr Kind sagt bei ㄇ sofort „m“ und bei ㄚ „a“, doch vor ㄇㄚ bleibt es stumm. Das ist kein Zeichen von Überforderung, sondern der bekannteste Engpass beim Zhuyin lernen: Zeichen kennen und Zeichen verbinden sind zwei verschiedene Fähigkeiten.
loc.answer: Wenn Ihr Kind die Zeichen kennt, aber keine Silbe liest, üben Sie das Verbinden getrennt: zuerst nur zwei Zeichen (Anlaut + Auslaut, z. B. ㄇㄚ), langsam gedehnt und dann schnell zusammen gesprochen, erst danach Silben mit Mittellaut wie ㄍㄨㄚ. Den Ton setzen Sie als letzten Schritt, wenn die Silbe ohne Ton sicher sitzt.
paras: Deutsche Kinder kennen dieses Prinzip oft schon aus der Grundschule: Laute werden „zusammengeschliffen“, bis ein Wort entsteht. Bei Zhuyin funktioniert es ähnlich, nur dass eine Silbe aus höchstens drei Zeichen besteht: einem Anlaut, manchmal einem Mittellaut (ㄧ, ㄨ, ㄩ) und einem Auslaut, dazu ein Tonzeichen. Wer alle 37 Zeichen einzeln abfragt, übt also nur den ersten Teil; das Lesen selbst entsteht erst beim Verbinden.

Hilfreich ist eine feste Reihenfolge der Schwierigkeit. Beginnen Sie mit Paaren, deren Anlaut sich dehnen lässt, etwa ㄇ, ㄈ, ㄙ oder ㄌ, weil das Kind den Übergang hören kann. Danach kommen Paare mit kurzen Anlauten wie ㄅ oder ㄉ und zuletzt Dreier-Silben mit Mittellaut. In Lumi Bopomofo verbindet der Lautzug genau diese Teile, Anlaut, Mittellaut und Auslaut, zu einer Silbe, sodass Ihr Kind das Zusammensetzen hört, bevor es selbst spricht.

Die Töne kommen am Schluss. Ein Kind, das ㄇㄚ sicher liest, kann anschließend mit der Ton-Achterbahn hören, wie dieselbe Silbe in unterschiedlichen Tönen klingt. Versucht man Silbe und Ton gleichzeitig, scheitert meist beides. Die tägliche Wiederholung holt Zeichen zurück, die noch wackeln, damit das Verbinden nicht an einem vergessenen Einzelzeichen hängt.
look: Werden Anlaut, Mittellaut und Auslaut hörbar zu einer Silbe verbunden?
Gibt es eigene Übungen für die Töne, getrennt vom Silbenlesen?
Holt eine Wiederholung unsichere Zeichen automatisch zurück?
Kann das Kind jedes Zeichen in der richtigen Strichfolge nachspuren?
Ist die App werbefrei, ohne Anmeldung und offline nutzbar?
steps: Prüfen Sie kurz, welche Einzelzeichen Ihr Kind schon sicher hört und erkennt.
Üben Sie zwei Wochen lang nur Zweier-Silben mit dehnbarem Anlaut, etwa ㄇㄚ, ㄈㄚ, ㄙㄚ.
Sprechen Sie jede Silbe erst langsam gedehnt, dann einmal schnell zusammen.
Nehmen Sie danach kurze Anlaute (ㄅ, ㄉ) und schließlich Silben mit Mittellaut wie ㄍㄨㄚ dazu.
Erst wenn die Silbe ohne Ton sitzt, dieselbe Silbe in verschiedenen Tönen hören lassen.
rows: Erkennen und Zusammenschleifen sind zwei Fähigkeiten
Kommen sie erst nach den Zweier-Silben?
Der Mittellaut ist der häufigste Stolperstein
Werden sie nach dem Silbenlesen eingeführt?
Silbe und Ton gleichzeitig überfordert die meisten Kinder
Ein wackelndes Zeichen blockiert die ganze Silbe
loc.fits: Lumi Bopomofo passt zu Familien, deren Kind die Zhuyin-Zeichen schon teilweise kennt und jetzt Silben lesen soll: Der Lautzug verbindet Anlaut, Mittellaut und Auslaut, die Ton-Achterbahn übt die Töne getrennt, und die tägliche Wiederholung holt unsichere Zeichen zurück. Dazu kommt Nachspuren in der richtigen Strichfolge. Ohne Werbung, ohne Anmeldung, offline spielbar; das erste Zeichen ausprobieren, dann alle 37 Zeichen mit einem einmaligen In-App-Kauf freischalten.
faq: Warum kann mein Kind alle Zeichen, aber kein Wort lesen?
Weil das Verbinden eine eigene Fähigkeit ist. Üben Sie es gezielt mit Zweier-Silben, statt weiter Einzelzeichen abzufragen.
Soll ich die Töne gleich mitlernen lassen?
Besser nicht gleichzeitig. Erst die Silbe ohne Ton sicher lesen, dann dieselbe Silbe in verschiedenen Tönen hören und sprechen.
Wie lange dauert der Schritt vom Zeichen zur Silbe?
Das ist sehr unterschiedlich. Mit zehn Minuten täglich merken viele Familien nach einigen Wochen, dass Zweier-Silben flüssiger werden; Dreier-Silben brauchen meist länger.

en.title: Learning zhuyin: your child knows the symbols but cannot read a syllable – what helps
en.meta: Many children recognise single bopomofo symbols but get stuck when blending them. How to join initial, medial and final into syllables at home, and add the tone only afterwards.
en.h1: Learning zhuyin: from single symbols to reading a syllable
en.lead: Your child says “m” for ㄇ and “a” for ㄚ straight away, then goes silent at ㄇㄚ. That is not a sign of overload; it is the best-known bottleneck in learning zhuyin: knowing symbols and joining them are two different skills.
en.answer: If your child knows the symbols but cannot read a syllable, practise blending on its own: first just two symbols (initial + final, such as ㄇㄚ), stretched slowly and then said quickly together, and only later syllables with a medial such as ㄍㄨㄚ. Add the tone as the last step, once the syllable is solid without it.
paras: Many children already know this idea from learning to read in school: sounds are blended until a word appears. Zhuyin works the same way, except that a syllable has at most three symbols: an initial, sometimes a medial (ㄧ, ㄨ, ㄩ) and a final, plus a tone mark. Quizzing all 37 symbols one by one only practises the first part; reading itself starts with joining them.

A fixed order of difficulty helps. Start with pairs whose initial can be stretched, such as ㄇ, ㄈ, ㄙ or ㄌ, because the child can hear the transition. Then move to pairs with short initials like ㄅ or ㄉ, and finally three-symbol syllables with a medial. In Lumi Bopomofo, the sound train joins exactly these parts, initial, medial and final, into one syllable, so your child hears the blend before saying it.

Tones come last. A child who reads ㄇㄚ confidently can then use the tone roller coaster to hear how the same syllable sounds in different tones. Trying syllable and tone at once usually makes both fail. The daily review brings back symbols that are still shaky, so blending does not stall on one forgotten symbol.

steps: Briefly check which single symbols your child already hears and recognises reliably.
For two weeks, practise only two-symbol syllables with a stretchable initial, such as ㄇㄚ, ㄈㄚ, ㄙㄚ.
Say each syllable slowly stretched first, then once quickly together.
Then add short initials (ㄅ, ㄉ) and finally syllables with a medial such as ㄍㄨㄚ.
Only when the syllable is solid without a tone, let your child hear the same syllable in different tones.

Tracing in the correct stroke order is included. No ads, no sign-up, playable offline; try the first symbol, then unlock all 37 with a single one-time in-app purchase.
faq: Why does my child know every symbol but cannot read a word?
Because blending is a separate skill. Practise it directly with two-symbol syllables instead of quizzing single symbols again.
Should tones be learned at the same time?
Better not at once. First read the syllable without a tone, then hear and say the same syllable in different tones.
How long does the step from symbol to syllable take?
It varies a lot. With ten minutes a day, many families notice two-symbol syllables getting smoother after a few weeks; three-symbol syllables usually take longer.

en.title: Your child forgets bopomofo right after learning it? Review only the mistaken symbols on paper
en.meta: When a child forgets bopomofo (zhuyin) a week later, it is usually because weak symbols are still mixed in. How to collect only the mistaken symbols and review them in the app and on printed sheets at home, plus what to check in a pay-once app.
en.h1: Bopomofo for kids: review only the mistaken symbols, in the app and on paper
en.lead: Bopomofo your child said fluently last week comes back only half as well this week. It is a common worry when teaching Taiwanese Mandarin at home. Repeating only the mistaken symbols, briefly, is easier on the child and on the parent than reviewing all 37 every time.
en.answer: If your child keeps forgetting bopomofo, stop repeating all 37 symbols; review only recently mistaken symbols in the app each day, and once or twice a week print just those symbols for tracing and a short test. For pairs with similar sounds, such as ㄓ and ㄗ, ㄕ and ㄙ, or ㄣ and ㄥ, add side-by-side listening practice.
paras: With only 37 symbols, bopomofo is often treated as done once everything has been learned. In practice, pairs with similar sounds keep getting mixed up. The retroflex ㄓ, ㄔ, ㄕ against the tongue-tip ㄗ, ㄘ, ㄙ, and the finals ㄣ and ㄥ, are sounds Japanese lacks, so children growing up in Japan confuse them easily. Reviewing everything evenly spends time on known symbols and thins out practice on the weak ones.

In Lumi Bopomofo Pro, today's review automatically brings back symbols that have not stuck yet. From the parent page, you can also print learned or recently mistaken symbols as tracing-plus-test sheets. The point is combining on-screen listening and choosing with writing in stroke order on paper, using the same weak symbols.

The printed sheets also work as a check before a weekend Mandarin class or before seeing grandparents. Circle the symbols written correctly and put the mistaken ones on next week's sheet again; that way the parent never has to make up questions. The app is fully unlocked with one purchase, with no ads and no in-app purchases, so a child can use it alone safely.

loc.title: 孩子寫字母老是寫反？b 和 d 分不清的起筆點練法
loc.meta: 三到七歲寫英文字母時把 b 寫成 d、p 寫成 q 很常見。用「從哪裡起筆、先直線還是先圓」來分，搭配筆順描寫與十字格，在家每天幾分鐘就能慢慢改過來。
loc.h1: 孩子寫字母老是寫反：用起筆點分清 b、d、p、q
loc.lead: 孩子寫字母時把 b 寫成 d、把 p 寫成 q，很多爸媽會擔心是不是學習有問題。其實這在七歲前非常常見：這幾個字母形狀一樣、只差方向，靠「看起來像什麼」去記，本來就容易反。
loc.answer: 孩子寫字母寫反時，不要只叫他「看清楚再寫」，而是固定每個字母的起筆點和第一筆：b 先寫直線再往右加圓，d 先寫圓再補右邊的直線。每天只練一對容易反的字母，照筆順描三次、在十字格裡自己寫兩次，寫反就回到起筆點重來。
paras: 小寫 b、d、p、q 是同一個形狀轉了方向，孩子記「一根棍子加一個圓」時，很難同時記住圓在哪一邊。如果每次寫的起筆位置都不一樣，手就沒有固定的動作可以依靠，寫反的機率就更高。把注意力從「長什麼樣子」換成「從哪裡開始、第一筆往哪走」，手的動作固定下來，方向自然跟著穩定。
練的時候一次只放一對，例如先練 b 和 d，穩了再換 p 和 q，不要四個一起。Lumi 字母星球 Lite 的大寫與小寫描寫都有筆順，十字輔助線帶著孩子一筆一筆描，起筆位置每次都一樣；描之前先聽字母的名字和發音，讓「/b/ 的聲音」和「先直線」綁在一起。
螢幕上描完，最好在紙上再寫一次，因為握筆寫在紙上才是孩子之後在學校要做的事。完整版可以一鍵匯出 PDF 學習單，自動帶入今天練過的字母與描寫格，印出來就能練。寫反時不用糾正很久，指著起筆點說「從這裡開始」，讓孩子重寫一次就好。

en.title: Your child keeps writing letters backwards? Fix b and d with the starting point
en.meta: Writing b as d or p as q is very common for children aged three to seven. Tell them apart by where the stroke starts and whether the line or the circle comes first, with stroke-order tracing and a guide grid, a few minutes a day at home.
en.h1: Your child writes letters backwards: use the starting point to tell b, d, p, q apart
en.lead: When a child writes b as d or p as q, many parents worry something is wrong. In fact it is very common before age seven: these letters share one shape and differ only in direction, so remembering them by how they look naturally leads to reversals.
en.answer: When your child writes letters backwards, do not just say “look carefully”; fix each letter's starting point and first stroke instead: b starts with the line and then adds the bump on the right, d starts with the circle and then adds the line on the right. Practise only one confusable pair a day: trace three times in stroke order, write twice in a guide grid, and if it reverses, start again from the starting point.
paras: Lowercase b, d, p and q are one shape turned in different directions. A child who remembers “a stick and a circle” struggles to also remember which side the circle goes on. If the starting point changes every time, the hand has no fixed movement to rely on, and reversals become more likely. Shifting attention from what it looks like to where it starts and where the first stroke goes fixes the hand movement, and direction follows.

Practise one pair at a time, such as b and d first, then p and q once those are steady, not all four together. In Lumi Letters Lite, uppercase and lowercase tracing both follow stroke order, and the cross guide lines walk the child through each stroke so the starting point is the same every time. Hearing the letter's name and sound before tracing ties the /b/ sound to “line first”.

After tracing on screen, writing once more on paper helps, because holding a pencil on paper is what school will ask for. The full version exports a PDF worksheet in one tap with today's letters and tracing boxes ready to print. When a letter reverses, there is no need for a long correction: point to the starting point, say “start here”, and let the child write it again.

faq: Is writing b as d a learning disability?

Reversals are very common before age seven, usually because the shapes are similar and direction is not fixed yet. If they are still frequent in the middle primary years, or come with reading difficulties, ask a teacher or specialist to assess.
Should I keep correcting reversals?
No long corrections are needed. Point to the starting point, say “start here”, and let your child write it once more; the goal is a well-practised first stroke.
Does tracing letters on an iPad help with writing on paper?
Tracing fixes stroke order and the starting point, but holding a pencil on paper still needs its own practice. Trace on screen, then write once on paper; doing both works best.

loc.title: Phonics cho bé đang học chữ tiếng Việt: làm sao để không lẫn âm “d”, “a”, “i”?
loc.meta: Bé vừa học chữ tiếng Việt vừa học phonics tiếng Anh dễ đọc lẫn vì cùng mặt chữ mà khác âm. Cách tách hai hệ âm ở nhà, chọn chữ cái nào học trước, mỗi ngày bao lâu, và điều cần kiểm tra ở ứng dụng mua một lần.
loc.h1: Phonics cho bé đang học chữ tiếng Việt: tách hai hệ âm cho rõ
loc.lead: Bé đọc chữ “d” trong tiếng Anh thành âm “d” của tiếng Việt, hoặc đọc “a” trong “cat” như “a” trong “ba”. Ba mẹ lo bé học phonics bị rối. Thực ra tiếng Việt và tiếng Anh dùng chung mặt chữ Latinh nhưng nhiều chữ đọc khác, nên lẫn âm lúc đầu là chuyện bình thường.
loc.answer: Khi dạy phonics cho bé đang học chữ tiếng Việt, hãy bắt đầu bằng những chữ đọc gần giống nhau ở hai thứ tiếng (như m, b, s, t) để bé tự tin, rồi mới đến các chữ khác âm như d, a, i; mỗi lần học tiếng Anh thì chỉ nghe và nói âm tiếng Anh, không giải thích bằng cách so với âm tiếng Việt. Mỗi ngày 10–15 phút là đủ.
paras: Chữ “d” trong tiếng Việt đọc gần như “z” (miền Bắc) hoặc “j” (miền Nam), còn “d” trong tiếng Anh lại gần với “đ”. Chữ “a” trong “cat” và “i” trong “sit” cũng là những âm ngắn mà tiếng Việt không có y hệt. Vì vậy nếu bé vừa vào lớp 1 học đánh vần tiếng Việt mà ba mẹ dạy cả 26 chữ phonics cùng lúc, bé dễ dùng âm tiếng Việt cho mặt chữ tiếng Anh.

Cách dễ nhất là tách bối cảnh: giờ tiếng Anh thì nghe giọng đọc tiếng Anh, chạm vào chữ để nghe âm, rồi tìm âm đó ở đầu, giữa hoặc cuối từ. Trong Lumi Letters Pro, bé nghe âm đầu, âm giữa và âm cuối của từ, ghép chữ hoa với chữ thường và tô từng chữ theo đường dẫn, nên mỗi chữ được gắn với âm tiếng Anh ngay từ đầu, không cần ba mẹ tự phát âm mẫu.

Ba mẹ không cần đoán bé đang yếu ở đâu. Trong khu vực dành cho phụ huynh, ba mẹ xem tiến bộ của bé ở bốn kỹ năng và in phiếu bài tập mỗi ngày để bé luyện thêm trên giấy. Lumi Letters Pro chỉ cần một lần mua: không quảng cáo, không gói đăng ký, không thu thập dữ liệu và chơi được khi không có mạng.

en.title: Phonics for a child learning Vietnamese letters: how to avoid mixing up “d”, “a”, “i”
en.meta: A child learning Vietnamese letters and English phonics at the same time easily mixes them up, because the letters look the same but sound different. How to keep the two sound systems apart at home, which letters to start with, how long per day, and what to check in a pay-once app.
en.h1: Phonics for a child learning Vietnamese letters: keep the two sound systems apart
en.lead: A child reads English “d” with the Vietnamese “d” sound, or says the “a” in “cat” like the “a” in Vietnamese “ba”. Parents worry phonics is confusing their child. In fact Vietnamese and English share Latin letters but read many of them differently, so early mix-ups are normal.
en.answer: When teaching phonics to a child who is learning Vietnamese letters, start with letters that sound similar in both languages (such as m, b, s, t) to build confidence, then move to letters that sound different, such as d, a, i. During English time, only hear and say English sounds, without explaining by comparison with Vietnamese. Ten to fifteen minutes a day is enough.
paras: Vietnamese “d” sounds close to “z” (north) or “j” (south), while English “d” is closer to Vietnamese “đ”. The “a” in “cat” and “i” in “sit” are short sounds Vietnamese does not have exactly. So if a child has just started first grade spelling in Vietnamese and parents teach all 26 phonics letters at once, the child easily applies Vietnamese sounds to English letters.

The easiest approach is separating the contexts: during English time, listen to an English voice, tap a letter to hear its sound, then find that sound at the beginning, middle or end of a word. In Lumi Letters Pro, the child hears the beginning, middle and end sounds of words, matches uppercase with lowercase and traces each letter along a guide, so every letter is tied to its English sound from the start without the parent having to model pronunciation.

Parents do not need to guess where the child is weak. In the parent area, they see progress across four skills and print a worksheet each day for extra practice on paper. Lumi Letters Pro needs only one purchase: no ads, no subscription, no data collection, and it plays offline.

A few sounds may get mixed at first, which is normal. Learning a few letters at a time and keeping English time and Vietnamese time clearly separate helps most children tell them apart gradually.

loc.title: กิจวัตรก่อนนอนของลูก: ทำไมทุกคืนยืดเยื้อ และวิธีจัดให้สั้นและเหมือนเดิมทุกคืน

loc.h1: กิจวัตรก่อนนอนของลูก: สั้น เรียงเดิม และเห็นว่าเหลืออีกกี่ขั้น

loc.answer: จัดกิจวัตรก่อนนอนให้เหลือ 3–4 ขั้นที่ทำเหมือนเดิมทุกคืน เช่น เก็บของเล่น → อาบน้ำ → แปรงฟัน → เข้านอน เริ่มเวลาเดิม และให้ลูกเห็นทันทีเมื่อทำแต่ละขั้นเสร็จ ผ่านไปหนึ่งสัปดาห์ให้ดูย้อนหลังว่าคืนไหนติดที่ขั้นไหน แล้วปรับเฉพาะขั้นนั้น ไม่ต้องเปลี่ยนทั้งชุด

หลังผ่านไปหนึ่งสัปดาห์ หน้าผู้ปกครองจะบันทึกทุกครั้งที่ทำสำเร็จพร้อมเวลา มีสรุปวันนี้และปฏิทิน 7 วัน ทำให้เห็นว่าคืนที่ยืดเยื้อมักติดที่ขั้นไหน เช่น แปรงฟันเสร็จช้ากว่าปกติในวันที่กลับบ้านดึก ถ้าอยากให้มีสัญญาณเริ่ม ตั้งแจ้งเตือนรายวัน (เลือกเปิดได้) ในเวลาที่เหมาะกับบ้านคุณ แอปซื้อครั้งเดียวใช้ได้ทุกอย่าง ไม่มีโฆษณา ไม่มีการซื้อในแอป และแชร์ในครอบครัวได้

en.title: Your child's bedtime routine: why every night drags on, and how to keep it short and the same
en.meta: Your child stalls before bed every night, even knowing teeth and toys come first. How to set a bedtime routine of 3–4 steps in the same order every night, let your child see how many steps are left, and look back at where it gets stuck.
en.h1: Your child's bedtime routine: short, in the same order, with the steps left visible
en.lead: It is 8 p.m. and your child still will not brush their teeth; once they do, they want to play a little longer, then ask for water and the toilet. A routine that should take twenty minutes takes over an hour. The problem is usually not stubbornness but not knowing what tonight involves and how much is left.
en.answer: Keep the bedtime routine to 3–4 steps done the same way every night, such as tidy toys → bath → brush teeth → bed, starting at the same time, and let your child see each step as done right away. After a week, look back at which step stalled on which night and adjust only that step, not the whole routine.
paras: Children aged three to seven cannot judge time yet, so “bedtime soon” means little to them. If the order changes each night, bath first today and teeth first tomorrow, every step becomes a negotiation. Few steps in the same order every night let the child know ahead that bed comes after brushing teeth, without a new argument each time.

Letting the child see progress for themselves helps a lot. Lumi Mission Planet Pro includes daily missions such as brushing teeth, tidying up and sleep, and unlimited custom missions such as “bath” or “choose one story”. Your child taps the screen each time a step is done, and their chosen buddy jumps to cheer right away. A tap takes only seconds, so a parent can hold the device and hand it over only when a step is finished.

After a week, the parent page has logged every completion with a timestamp, with a today summary and a 7-day calendar, showing which step usually drags on long nights, for example teeth taking longer on days you get home late. For a start signal, set an optional daily reminder at a time that suits your family. The app is a one-time purchase that unlocks everything, with no ads, no in-app purchases, and Family Sharing support.

loc.lead: Ein Agent, der eine Stunde lang refaktoriert, bricht nicht an der schwierigen Stelle ab, sondern dort, wo das Limit endet. Meist hätte ein kurzer Blick vorher gereicht.

paras: Wer nach „Codex Limit“ sucht, ist oft gerade mitten in einer Aufgabe gestoppt worden. ChatGPT Codex zählt die Nutzung in einem 5-Stunden-Fenster und in einem Wochenfenster. Das 5-Stunden-Fenster ist nach wenigen Stunden wieder frei, das Wochenfenster nicht. Ein langer Agentenlauf, der beide stark belastet, kann deshalb an einem Dienstag die halbe Woche kosten.
